actionable feedback for Product, Engineering, and other cross-functional teams.</li> <li value="8">Partner with internal stakeholders to ensure customer feedback, feature requests, and adoption insights inform roadmap priorities and improvements to the overall customer experience.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Strong understanding of DevSecOps practices, with the ability to connect GitLab capabilities across source code management, CI/CD, security, and Agile planning to tangible business outcomes.</li> <li value="2">Experience leading and developing technical teams in a distributed, remote environment, with a focus on customer outcomes and scalable impact.</li> <li value="3">Background in software development or engineering that enables you to guide technical conversations, remove adoption barriers, and design effective enablement paths.</li> <li value="4">Experience designing and implementing scalable customer success or technical enablement programs, using data to measure impact and refine approaches.</li> <li value="5">Ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, outcome-focused messaging for both technical and title: Senior Data Scientist (Credit)
description: <p><strong>Who we are</strong></p> <p>Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. </p> <p>As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.</p> <p> </p> <p><strong>About the role: </strong></p> <p>At Moniepoint, data is at the core of everything we do. We are a customer-centric company, and your work will enable our teams to make informed, data-driven decisions that directly impact the success of our business. We are seeking a data-driven, impact-oriented Senior Data Scientist to power Moniepoint’s consumer lending decisions at scale. You will build the models, experiments, and insights that shape how we acquire, underwrite, and retain millions of customers across Nigeria and Africa.</p> <p>This role is pivotal in driving our pricing, credit limit modelling, and credit model deployment strategy in a growing business with unparalleled opportunities to give access to millions of customers. You’ll collaborate with our amazing Consumer Credit team and drive how we think about risk ranking, product offering, and data infrastructure to create the best personalised offers for our customers. You’ll be responsible for building our first suite of credit risk models and help drive a culture of how we should think about machine learning vs more traditional methods - bringing fresh thinking to inspire both the team and our customers.</p> <p>Sitting at the intersection of data science, credit risk, and product, you’ll translate complex data into actionable decisions that drive growth with healthy portfolio performance.</p> <p><em>Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? <a href="https://moniepoint.com/blog">Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth.</a></em></p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop and deploy credit scoring, affordability, and behavioural models to support underwriting, pricing, and collections</li> <li>Design and run experiments to optimise approval rates, loss rates, and profitability</li> <li>Partner with product squads to embed decision logic into real-time systems</li> <li>Ensure data quality, compliance, and ethical use of models across all decisioning processes</li> <li>Mentor product squads on best practices in experimentation and data-driven decision-making</li> <li>Provide models to optimise outcomes in collections, churn management and user retention</li> </ul> <p><strong>We would love to hear from you if…</strong></p> <ul> <li>You’re comfortable with Statistics and have a Degree or qualifications  in a quantitative field (Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering or similar)</li> <li>You have +5 years of experience in data science, decision science, or risk analytics within financial services</li> <li>Working knowledge of credit risk, consumer lending, and regulatory considerations</li> <li>Proficiency in SQL and at least one modelling/programming language (Python, R)</li> <li>Experience with A/B testing, machine learning, collections modelling and churn management</li> <li>Ability to translate complex analyses into clear recommendations for business stakeholders</li> <li>High ownership mindset and comfort working in fast-paced, cross-functional teams</li> </ul> <p><strong>What we can offer you</strong></p> <ul> <li>Culture: We put our people first and prioritise the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human.</li> <li>Learning: We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks.</li> <li>Compensation: You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, monthly bonuses, plus other benefits</li> </ul> <p><strong>What to expect in the hiring process</strong></p> <ul> <li>A preliminary phone call with the recruiter</li> <li>A coding exercise on HackerRank - covering core data science theory (math, statistics, linear algebra) and Python fundamentals (data structures & algorithms).</li> <li>A take-home assignment</li> <li>A technical interview with a Lead in our Data Science Team to review your take-home assignment in depth</li> <li>A behavioural and technical interview with the hiring manager</li> </ul> <p><em>Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.</em></p> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Head of Engineering, Rewards
description: <p><strong>Who we are</strong></p> <p>Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. </p> <p>As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.</p> <p><strong>Why United Kingdom</strong></p> <p>The UK is home to our headquarters where more than 70 team members are based. Our London office is located at Sea Containers, just by London Bridge - this is also where a significant number of our most senior leaders sit, which makes it a natural base for a Head of Engineering.</p> <p>So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Rewards to join us in United Kingdom.</p> <p><strong>About The Role</strong></p> <p>Rewards is one of the most strategically important platforms at Moniepoint, and it is being built into a dedicated charter with its own engineering and product leadership. The platform sits at the centre of our retention strategy across a user base of approximately 23 million people.</p> <p>Today the platform does one thing: cashback. It works, but it has barely scratched the surface of what rewards can be, and the cashback product itself is not yet built to the depth it deserves. The ambition is to evolve it into a full rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform — and to do that across the full 360 degrees of our network. That means rewards for our business customers, rewards for our consumer customers, and rewards for the sales agents who drive our distribution. Very few companies get to design this from close to a blank page at this scale.</p> <p>The Head of Engineering owns that platform end to end. You will inherit a team of nine engineers, including an Engineering Manager, and build the organisation out from there — the current expectation is a minimum of three product units and upwards of 25 people, though the eventual shape is genuinely yours to define. Your first objective is to get the best possible performance out of the cashback product we already have. From there, you will work with Growth, Sales and Marketing to determine what we build for acquisition and retention, and roll it out across every customer we serve.</p> <p>This is a consumer-facing product engineering role, and that is the most important thing to understand about it. Rewards is won or lost on experimentation, personalisation, and the quality of the experience in a customer's hands. We are looking for a leader who has built and shipped direct-to-consumer products at scale, who is fluent in experimentation and A/B testing, and who has real depth in front-end and mobile engineering — not a purely backend platform leader.</p> <p>Moniepoint runs a Domain CTO model. We view our Heads of Engineering as the CTO of their domain: you own the technical roadmap, the architecture, the delivery, and the organisation beneath you. You will have full autonomy over engineering strategy, architecture, hiring, operating cadence and roadmap trade-offs.</p> <p>You will report functionally to our Group CTO, with a dual reporting line into the Product leader for Rewards. That second line is a delivery relationship rather than a seniority one — engineering and product are peers here, and you will build the team to full capacity together. Your responsibilities as Head of Engineering, Rewards includes:</p> <ul> <li>Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Rewards Platform end to end.</li> <li>Improving the performance, reliability and depth of the existing cashback product as an immediate first priority.</li> <li>Evolving cashback into a broader rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform serving business customers, consumer customers and sales agents.</li> <li>Building the engineering organisation from its current base - structuring product units, hiring engineers and Engineering Managers, and leading through those managers as the team scales.</li> <li>Establishing a strong experimentation culture: A/B testing, cohort analysis, and measurement that lets the team learn quickly what actually changes customer behaviour.</li> <li>Working closely with Growth, Sales and Marketing to translate acquisition and retention objectives into product and engineering initiatives.</li> <li>Owning the customer-facing experience of rewards across mobile and web, including how quickly and reliably customers receive what they have earned.</li> <li>Define architecture standards, engineering processes and quality metrics, and own the engineering health of the domain — incidents, production defects, deployment frequency, change failure rate, and developer experience.</li> <li>Build the platform to serve customers across multiple geographies as Moniepoint expands.</li> <li>Partner with Product to define the rewards-specific metrics and OKRs that do not yet exist, and hold the team to them.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Who You Are </strong></p> <ul> <li>Direct-to-consumer product engineering at scale. You have built and shipped products used directly by large consumer audiences, and you understand what moves engagement and retention. This is the defining requirement of the role.</li> <li>Genuine front-end and mobile depth. You have led or personally built consumer-facing mobile and web experiences. A backend-only background, however strong, is not what this role needs.</li> <li>Experimentation and growth engineering. Hands-on experience running A/B tests, feature flagging, and measurement frameworks, and using the results to drive product decisions rather than to justify them.</li> <li>At least 5 years of experience managing managers — leading an engineering organisation through other engineering leaders, not a single team.</li> <li>Hands-on technical leadership. You are still close to the code. We expect a meaningful proportion of hands-on engineering time and technical credibility with the engineers you lead.</li> <li>10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with at least 5 years leading engineering teams through growth phases.</li> <li>Comfort with our backend environment — Java and Spring Boot — and the ability to lead backend engineers credibly, even if it is not where your own depth sits.</li> <li>Experience building and scaling an engineering organisation from a small base, including hiring and developing Engineering Managers.</li> <li>Strong collaboration with commercial stakeholders — growth, marketing and sales — and the ability to translate business objectives into engineering work.</li> <li>Rewards, loyalty, gamification, personalisation or growth platform experience is a strong advantage but is not required.</li> <li>Fintech or payments experience is an advantage, not a requirement.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Cultural Alignment</strong></p> <p>As well, we assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation.</p> <ul> <li>Customer Obsession: Build deep empathy for users. Solve problems intuitively, and fix root causes, not just tickets.</li> <li>Craft: Master the fundamentals. Reason from first principles, make trade-offs explicit, and raise the bar on quality.</li> <li>Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality.</li> <li>Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. title: Business Process Lead, Finance & Corporate Services
description: About Kaseya Kaseya is the leading provider of AI-powered IT management and cybersecurity software, serving Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and internal IT organizations worldwide. Our comprehensive platform helps organizations efficiently manage, secure, and automate their IT environments, driving operational efficiency and long-term business success. Today, Kaseya supports customers in more than 20 countries and manages over 15 million endpoints worldwide. Founded in 2000, Kaseya was built by builders - and we're still building. We look for people who create rather than wait, who see a hard problem and lean in, and who treat challenges as raw material. At Kaseya, everyone plays a role in shaping the future of IT: whether you're in engineering, product, sales, marketing, customer support, or operations, your work helps protect, defend, and optimize IT environments across the globe. We're building teams that grow, perform, and make an impact. If you're driven by the itch to make things better - a product, a process, a career - you'll fit right in. At Kaseya, we don't just raise the bar. We build it. Position Summary The Business Process Lead, Finance & Corporate Services owns the end-to-end design of our financial and administrative back-office processes — financial close and reporting, procurement, tax, supply chain operations, hardware fulfillment, human resources operations, and sales compensation administration. This scope is intentionally broad rather than a single linear process flow, spanning several distinct domains that share a finance and administrative reporting line rather than a common process sequence. The role is the connective tissue between Finance, HR, and Supply Chain leadership and the technology teams that build supporting systems. Importantly, this role owns the business capabilities in this scope — their definition, design, decomposition, and governance — in close partnership with the business teams that operate the underlying functions day to day. It does not own those functions themselves; success depends on heavy partnership with business and technology leads rather than on direct authority. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role: the person hired personally facilitates working sessions, maps processes, writes requirements, and stays engaged through delivery and adoption. It also sits within a newly created function whose standards and operating rhythm are still being defined. Deep specialist expertise in every domain within this scope is not expected; the ability to establish consistent standards, prioritize effectively, and drive improvement across genuinely different process areas is the core skill this role requires. Key Responsibilities Own and continuously maintain a detailed (L2/L3) decomposition of Record to Report, Direct Tax and Tax Compliance, Procure to Pay, Supply Chain Operations, hardware fulfillment, Hire to Retire, and Sales Compensation Management capabilities, keeping documentation accurate as the operating model and systems landscape evolve, and using standards shared across the Business Process Lead team. Facilitate structured working sessions with Finance, HR, Procurement, and Supply Chain stakeholders to document how processes work today and design how they should work going forward, producing process maps, documented decisions, and requirements a technical team can act on without extensive follow-up. Translate future-state process designs into system requirements, partner with Product Owners and Engineering Leads through design, build, and testing, and confirm that what gets delivered reflects the intended process design. Support two parallel delivery tracks — current, in-production systems and the next-generation platform build — correctly identifying which track an incoming request belongs to, and ensuring lessons learned in day-to-day operations are reflected back into documentation and forward-looking design work. Own change management, enablement, and adoption for process changes in this value stream — stakeholder impact assessment, readiness planning, training materials, and post-launch verification that new processes are being used as intended — and define and report the process performance metrics that show whether they are working. Hold and maintain documented agreements at shared boundaries with peer Business Process Leads, so handoffs between value streams are explicitly agreed rather than assumed. Own the capability design for sales compensation from an approved sales quota forward — plan administration, crediting rules, attainment calculation, dispute resolution, commission expense accrual, and the payout handoff to payroll — partnering with the Sales Compensation and Payroll teams who execute it. Own the capability design for hardware fulfillment — provisioning, warehouse and inventory management, returns, and warranty — and for Hire to Retire, including onboarding, self-service, HR helpdesk, absence, and performance management, partnering with the Supply Chain, Fulfillment Operations, HR, and People Operations teams who run them. Required Qualifications Hands-on experience designing or improving month-end close and record-to-report processes in a multi-entity ERP environment. 5+ years of experience in business process design, business analysis, business architecture, or operations in a relevant domain. Demonstrated experience decomposing business capabilities into detailed, multi-level structures. Strong facilitation skills with cross-functional business stakeholders, including experience working at a Controller or Finance director level. Experience translating business process requirements into system requirements for a technical delivery team, along with strong documentation habits. Preferred Qualifications Experience with physical fulfillment and supply chain process design — warehouse, inventory, returns processing, and warranty management. Sales compensation process design experience, including plan administration, crediting, attainment, dispute resolution, and commission accounting. Procure-to-pay process design experience, including intake, approval routing, supplier onboarding, and three-way match controls. Direct tax process and statutory reporting experience in a multi-jurisdiction environment. HR operations process design experience, including onboarding, self-service, helpdesk operations, and performance cycle management. Treasury and cash management process design experience. Experience with Oracle (accounting, inventory, and accounts payable modules), NetSuite, Oracle EPM, close management tooling such as FloQast, and incentive compensation platforms such as CaptivateIQ. title: Director, Information Security
description: About Carrot : Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide. Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com . The Opportunity Carrot is looking for a Director, Information Security to lead the security program that protects the highly sensitive fertility and family-building data of members around the world. You will set the security strategy, own both corporate security (GRC, incident response, security awareness, vendor risk) and product security (application, cloud and infrastructure security, secure development lifecycle), and serve as the trusted voice on Carrot's security posture with executives, auditors, and enterprise customers. Day to day, you will balance setting direction with staying close to the work: prioritizing risk with Engineering and IT, guiding audit and certification cycles, coaching a small and talented team, and joining customer conversations where security is part of the buying decision. Carrot has already earned SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, HITRUST, and PCI DSS compliance, so this role is about taking a strong foundation to the next level of maturity, not starting from scratch. What makes this role different is the combination of stakes and influence. Few security leaders get to protect data this personal, at global scale, while working directly with executive leadership and shaping how a health platform is built, sold, and trusted. What You’ll Own In this role, you will: Lead Carrot's security strategy and roadmap, using a recognized maturity model (such as C2M2 or NIST CSF) to prioritize investments and report progress to executive leadership Own the full security program across corporate security (GRC, incident management, security awareness, third-party risk) and product security (application security, cloud and infrastructure security, secure SDLC) Partner with Engineering, especially the Internal Platform team, to build security into how Carrot designs, ships, and operates its systems, going beyond compliance Lead internal risk assessments across application, cloud, and corporate environments and turn the results into prioritized technical safeguards Own the compliance portfolio, including SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS, and HIPAA, and prepare Carrot for additional frameworks such as ISO 27001 as the business requires Direct incident response readiness, including playbooks, tabletop exercises, executive communication, and post-incident learning Represent Carrot's security posture to employers, health plans, and health systems through security reviews, questionnaires, and strategic sales conversations Work with Legal and Privacy to meet global data protection requirements (HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA/CPRA) for member health data Build, coach, and grow the security team, balancing hands-on execution with delegation as the team scales Manage the security budget, tooling, and vendor relationships, and tailor security guidance for a remote-first workforce and physical offices What Success Looks Like In your first 12–18 months, you will have: A documented, executive-endorsed security strategy and multi-year roadmap with clear priorities, owners, and measures of progress Clean outcomes on recurring audits and certifications (SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS), with remediation items closed on schedule A tested incident response program, with regular tabletop exercises completed and lessons learned built back into the program A measurable reduction in high-risk vulnerabilities and open security findings, with remediation timelines agreed on with Engineering A living risk register and vendor security review process that leaders rely on to make decisions A security team with defined roles, clear growth paths, and the right capacity for Carrot's growth, including key hires made Faster, more consistent security reviews for Sales and Customer Success, with fewer escalations from enterprise customers A clear plan, and visible progress, on any additional frameworks the business prioritizes, such as ISO 27001 About You ✨ You likely have: A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent experience) 10+ years of experience in technology, including 5+ years in information security and at least 3 years leading security teams A security certification such as CISSP or CISM Experience leading the security function at a late-stage startup, scale-up, or public company Working depth in healthcare data protection and privacy frameworks, including HIPAA, GDPR, and CCPA/CPRA Experience overseeing enterprise frameworks and audits such as SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS, and ISO 27001 Strong knowledge of application, network, and cloud security (AWS and Azure) and frameworks such as NIST CSF and OWASP Experience running core security programs, including incident response, risk management, vulnerability management, penetration testing, and security awareness Executive-level communication skills and confidence engaging customers and sales teams on security requirements Experience managing budget and allocating resources across people, tools, and vendors Nice to Have ⭐ While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring: Experience leading security through a major company event such as an IPO, acquisition, or large-scale audit cycle A background in healthcare, digital health, or another highly regulated, high-trust environment Experience leading security in a remote-first, globally distributed company Familiarity with compliance automation platforms such as Drata Experience building a security engineering practice alongside platform and infrastructure teams Why This Role Matters Members trust Carrot with some of the most personal information a person can share, often during some of the most meaningful moments of their lives. Protecting that trust is not a back-office function. It is what allows employers, health plans, and health systems to bring Carrot to millions of people worldwide. As Carrot grows, security leadership shapes how we build, how we sell, and how we show up for customers. In this role, you will make security a strength that members and customers can see and rely on, and build a team that keeps raising the bar as the business scales. Why Candidates Join Carrot Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission. Highlights include: A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally. A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact. Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits. Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge. Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits. A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture. The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide. Compensation: Carrot offers a holistic Total Rewards package designed to support our employees in all aspects of their lives inside and outside of work, including health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, short- and long-term incentives, parental leave, family-forming assistance, and a competitive compensation package. The starting base salary for this position will range from $188,000.00 - $245,000.00. Actual compensation may vary from posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience. If you receive messages from any other domain, please disregard them and report the incident to: securityreporting@get-carrot.com A Note on AI At Carrot, we believe AI can help us work smarter, move faster, and create more meaningful experiences for our members, customers, and each other. While not every role requires deep technical AI expertise, we value people who are curious, eager to learn, and excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI into their day-to-day work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement—and we'll call that out clearly in the qualifications. For everyone else, we're looking for people who embrace new ways of working, use AI responsibly to improve quality and efficiency, and continue to learn as the technology evolves. Why Carrot? description: Built's Mission: Connect and simplify doing business in real estate. Built is the AI-powered platform transforming the way real estate is financed, developed, and managed. Today, Built is a partner to more than 350 lenders, over 80,000 borrowers and owners, and thousands of contractors, powering 86,000 active projects valued at more than $300 billion. Learn more at getbuilt.com . __________________________ Built Technologies is transforming how capital moves through construction and real estate finance - one of the largest, most complex sectors in the economy. Our platform connects lenders, including many of the top U.S. banks, with the owners, developers, and general contractors they finance. When a draw is approved, a builder can pay subcontractors. When a compliance document clears, a project moves forward. The work we do here is not abstract; it has a direct and material impact on how capital flows and how real estate gets built. Our Implementations team delivers the platform experiences that determine whether a lender adopts Built as their operational backbone or walks away. As an Implementation Consultant II, you will manage a strategic portfolio of complex client implementations with growing independence; owning end-to-end delivery for enterprise-scale lending clients and beginning to contribute to how the broader team operates. You bring a track record of successful go-lives, strong client relationships, and the judgment to navigate novel challenges without constant direction. This role supports owners, developers, and general contractors and is especially well suited to someone who brings construction context plus the ability to learn and deliver software. Our Guiding Principles Be Bold. We pursue the biggest problems in our industry, challenge assumptions others take for granted, and take calculated risks to get there. We don't hide behind consensus or committees. Playing it safe is just failing slowly. Help Customers Win. We learn our customers' businesses deeply — how they think, how they deploy capital, what keeps them up at night. We treat their capital like our own. We ship leverage, not features. And we measure ourselves by customer results, not our intentions. Move with Urgency & Purpose. We bias toward delivery over perfection, remove friction from our own paths, and communicate in real time. Momentum compounds — and we build it every day. Own the Outcome. We own outcomes, not just tasks. We hold a high Say:Do ratio and take responsibility from idea through impact. When something breaks, we fix it — we don't wait to be asked. Never Satisfied. We raise the bar continuously. We stay curious, hold exacting standards, debate hard, and hold our opinions loosely when the evidence shifts. Excellence is a habit, not an event. What You'll Do Lead complex implementations for owner, developer, and general contractor clients - managing project scope, risk, and timeline with meaningful autonomy and clear accountability for outcomes. Conduct discovery and planning sessions with client stakeholders, translating strategic business goals and workflows into actionable implementation roadmaps. Manage escalations and navigate organizational dynamics on the client side, driving timely resolution of high-impact issues with composure and authority. Identify process improvements and standardization opportunities across your implementation portfolio — document repeatable solutions and share them with the broader team. Contribute to cross-functional initiatives with Sales, Product, and Engineering to improve implementation efficiency, reduce time-to-value, and strengthen client outcomes. Track and communicate implementation metrics, insights, and lessons learned to leadership and the broader team; use data to surface patterns and drive improvement. Leverage AI tools to accelerate project planning, client communication, and risk identification across your portfolio. What You'll Bring 2-4 years of experience in SaaS implementation, professional services, or enterprise project delivery, ideally in construction technology, financial services, fintech, or a complex B2B software environment. Construction industry experience is strongly preferred. You have worked for or closely with an owner, developer, general contractor, subcontractor, or construction technology company, and understand the operational realities of running projects. A proven ability to deliver concurrent client implementations on time and to a high standard, with examples of measurable client outcomes you drove. Strong client communication and relationship management skills; you navigate senior stakeholders, handle difficult conversations with confidence, and build trust through consistent follow-through. A track record of identifying process improvements that made implementations faster, more consistent, or more successful for clients. Working knowledge of construction project and financial workflows, such as project set-up, project financials, payables, lien waivers, project controls, or subcontractor/vendor coordination. You can use that context to help a customer translate how they work today into a practical workflow in Built. Some experience with implementation methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid approaches) and comfort adapting your approach to the client's environment. Comfort with project management tools, CRM systems, and analytics platforms; ability to learn new tools quickly and apply them effectively. What Success Looks Like at Six Months Your implementation portfolio is delivering consistently — projects are on schedule, clients are satisfied, and go-lives are producing measurable adoption outcomes. You've successfully navigated at least one high-complexity or high-risk implementation to a successful go-live, demonstrating sound judgment under pressure. You've contributed at least one process improvement or documented playbook that has been adopted by the broader implementations team. Cross-functional partners in Sales, Product, and Engineering consistently seek your input when complex client situations arise, trusting your judgment and domain expertise. Apply AI to sharpen decision-making and strengthen strategic insights. Share effective AI use cases and best practices with your team. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Subject Matter Expert (SME), you'll be the deepest technical voice in the field for one product group, helping customers make technical decisions on GitLab's most important opportunities, roughly the top 10% by size or complexity.</p> <p>Account Solutions Architects (Account SAs) will bring you into prioritized opportunities. The Account SA owns the opportunity; you own your product group's success within it. You'll work directly with Product and Engineering, bringing customer needs and field insights into roadmap discussions. You'll also help the wider Solutions Architecture team build expertise through reusable assets, enablement, and coaching.</p> <p>You'll specialize in one product group, not all four. In Security & Compliance, you'll focus on GitLab Ultimate, application security, Dependency Firewall, software supply chain security, compliance, and artificial intelligence (AI) governance. In Platform, you'll focus on GitLab Dedicated, self-managed deployments, bring your own model, and cloud and hybrid architecture. In Core DevSecOps, you'll focus on GitLab Premium, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), source code management, Orbit, Artifact Central, and migrations. DevSecOps brings development, security, and operations together across software delivery. In AI & Competitive, you'll focus on GitLab Duo Agent Platform, agentic workflows, AI-native development, competitive displacement including GitHub, and migrations.</p> <p>Your success will be measured by technical win rate and bookings on SME-engaged opportunities, product-category commit attainment and consumption growth in your region, and Proof of Value (PoV) conversion rate, evaluation cycle time, and time from technical win to production use. We'll also measure how often Account SAs reuse your assets, their confidence in handling your product group without escalation, and the quality and impact of your feedback to Product.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Act as the technical authority for your product group on prioritized opportunities, from discovery and architecture through trials and PoV evaluations.</li> <li>Lead technical deep dives, workshops, and executive briefings that connect product capabilities to business outcomes and explain how GitLab differs from competing solutions.</li> <li>Design and improve standardized PoV templates with clear, repeatable success criteria. Account SAs own the customer PoV; you'll contribute product-specific content and expertise while keeping the evaluation connected to the broader GitLab platform.</li> <li>Equip account teams for product launches with Product Management and Product Marketing. Build demos and talk tracks, and turn early customer wins into reference stories.</li> <li>Serve as the escalation point for Account SAs and Post-Sales Solutions Architects (Post-Sales SAs) on complex product questions, integrations, and objections.</li> <li>Hand off PoV success criteria and architecture decisions to the Post-Sales SA with the account team when an opportunity closes. Stay involved until the customer's first production workload uses the product, and support complex accounts when Post-Sales SAs bring you in to drive adoption and consumption.</li> <li>Bring structured field feedback, competitive insights, and customer requirements to Product Management and Engineering with the wider SME team. Help manage early-access and design-partner programs, and represent GitLab through customer events, conferences, industry working groups, and published content.</li> <li>Build reference architectures, demo environments, competitive battlecards, PoV playbooks, and enablement content so account teams can handle more opportunities without your direct involvement. Mentor Account SAs and contribute to GitLab's global SME community of practice.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Substantial experience in technical pre-sales, solutions architecture, consulting, or software engineering, with deep, hands-on expertise in one domain: application security testing, supply chain security, and compliance; scalable cloud and hybrid platforms; large CI/CD environments and source code migrations; or production AI-assisted development, working prototypes, and competitive evaluations.</li> <li>Practical expertise in agentic and AI-assisted development workflows across planning, coding, testing, security, and delivery, applied in a customer-facing, pre-sales context.</li> <li>Experience winning technical decisions on large, complex enterprise opportunities through structured Proof of Concept (PoC) or PoV evaluations with defined success criteria and executive sign-off.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with Git, CI/CD, containers, Kubernetes, and at least one major cloud provider.</li> <li>The ability to lead a whiteboard session with engineers and present the business case to executives in the same meeting.</li> <li>Strong written communication, including the ability to turn complex topics into clear playbooks that others use.</li> <li>Comfort working asynchronously across time zones with Sales, Product, and Engineering.</li> <li>Optional: public speaking, published technical content, open source contributions, or relevant certifications in Kubernetes, cloud architecture, or security.</li> </ul> <p>If you bring transferable experience in an adjacent domain, we encourage you to apply.</p> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>We're building our SME organization within GitLab's Solutions Architecture team, and we're distributed and all-remote.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a title: Sustainability Account Associate - Junior Level (all genders)
description: JOIN US Bei Code Gaia zu arbeiten bedeutet, dass du an etwas sehr Wichtigem arbeitest: Der Transformation zu einer nachhaltigen Wirtschaft. Unser Ziel ist es, eine praktische Lösung anzubieten und Unternehmen dabei zu helfen, die Arbeitsabläufe im Nachhaltigkeitsmanagement und -reporting zu automatisieren und gleichzeitig für sie einen wirtschaftlichen Mehrwert zu schaffen. Aufgrund unserer steigenden Kundenzahlen, sowie der bevorstehenden Gesetzgebung brauchen wir Verstärkung im Team und würden dich gerne dabei haben. description: Hopkins ist eine auf die Rechte von Privatpersonen spezialisierte, deutschlandweit tätige Kanzlei. title: Director, GTM Finance
description: About Customer.io Over 9,000 companies — from scrappy startups to global brands — use our platform to send billions of emails, push notifications, in-app messages, and SMS every day. Customer.io powers automated communication that people actually want to receive. We help teams send smarter, more relevant messages using real-time behavioral data. About the role Hi, my name is Diep Nguyen, VP of Finance here at Customer.io , and I'm looking for a Director, GTM Finance to own our go-to-market P&L end-to-end as we scale from $100M+ ARR today to $1B+ ARR in the future. We're hiring for strategic finance horsepower first: someone who builds models from a blank page, challenges assumptions, and earns trust with senior executives. Deep GTM fluency matters just as much — but for a strong finance generalist, that business partnership often shows up in the work rather than the title. You'll own our GTM P&L spanning Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success, and build the team behind it. We're an AI-forward company: this role requires someone energized by using AI to reinvent how finance operates, not someone who merely tolerates the tools we hand them. What we value Financial rigor over title-matching — we care more about how you've built and defended models than whether "GTM Finance" was ever your title. AI as genuine practice, not a buzzword — we want concrete stories of AI changing an outcome, not familiarity with the tools. Ownership from day one — you'll build and lead a team, not just execute analysis handed to you. Directness with data — you challenge top-down assumptions with account-level evidence, even in uncomfortable conversations. What you’ll do Own the GTM P&L end-to-end — revenue, gross margin, and opex across Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success — not just a spend-efficiency lens. Drive unit economics and the growth funnel model — CAC, LTV/CAC, payback, magic number, and cohort/retention analysis across self-serve and sales-assisted motions. Own the ARR roll-forward, bookings, and revenue forecasting — auditable, reconcilable, and independently stress-tested against top-down assumptions. Partner with Sales and RevOps on capacity planning, deal economics, and pricing — protecting margin and ARR quality without slowing deal velocity. Build and own the monthly/quarterly GTM reporting package for the exec team and Board, with variance analysis that explains root cause. Champion AI-enabled finance workflows and build the GTM finance team as Customer.io scales past $250M+ ARR. What we're looking for 10+ years in FP&A, strategic finance, or related roles at complex, scaled orgs; a first-principles modeler who builds from a blank page rather than inheriting assumptions Deep GTM business-partnering experience with Sales, Marketing, or Customer Success — regardless of whether "GTM Finance" was ever the title Comfortable with subscription/SaaS metrics (ARR, NRR, CAC, LTV) or able to get there fast Concrete, demonstrated track record driving AI adoption in finance workflows — not just familiarity with the tools Proven people leader — has managed and developed finance professionals Strong Excel skills (with experience using Snowflake a plus) and experience with planning/GTM systems (NetSuite, Salesforce, Gong, Drivetrain) Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field; MBA a plus Compensation & Benefits We believe in transparency. Starting salary for this role is $200K–$255K USD (or equivalent in local currency) depending on experience and subject to market rate adjustment. We know our people are what make us great, and we’re committed to taking great care of them. Our inclusive benefits package supports your well-being and growth, including 100% coverage of medical, dental, vision, mental health, and supplemental insurance premiums for you and your family . We also offer 16 weeks paid parental leave, unlimited PTO , stipends for remote work and wellness, a professional development budget, and more. See full benefits here → Our Process No gotchas, no trick questions - just a clear, human process designed to help both of us make an informed decision. Recruiter Screen (30 min) Hiring Manager Screen (45 min) Two Cross-functional conversations with team members (30 min each) Case study + Case Review Panel with team (45 min) All final candidates will be asked to complete a background check and employment verifications as part of our pre-employment process. Customer.io recognizes the stifling impact of systemic injustice on diverse communities. We commit to using our influence to increase inclusion and equity within the tech industry. We strive to build an inclusive team culture, implement bias-free hiring practices, and develop community partnerships to expand our global impact. Zoom is the only video conference platform that we use, virtual interviews will be conducted using the video capability (i.e., not via the chat), and offers will be extended in writing on official Customer.io letterhead. Please be vigilant in all of your job search activity, and if you have any questions please contact jobs@customer.io . Join us! Check out our careers page for more information about why you should come work with us! We believe in empathy, transparency, responsibility, and, yes, a little awkwardness. If you’re excited by what you read — apply now.

title: Senior Sales Operations & Compensation Manager
description: About Us Wrapbook is the AI platform for production finance. We’re building a system of action that puts finance teams in control of their whole production, from payroll, to spend, to accounting. Built for feature films, TV, and commercials, Wrapbook is trusted by teams at Netflix, Paramount, Anonymous Content, and more. With backing from Andreessen Horowitz, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Jeffrey Katzenberg's WndrCo, our team of 350+ is using AI to transform how finance teams work and empower them to do more with less. The Opportunity — (Remote - USA / CANADA) We are looking for a Senior Sales Operations & Compensation Manager to serve as the embedded operational partner to our Sales organization. Reporting to the Head of Revenue Operations, you'll own the Salesforce data layer, forecasting cadences, compensation administration, and deal desk processes that power Wrapbook's go-to-market engine across SMB, Mid-Market, and Enterprise segments. This is a high-autonomy role where your work directly impacts revenue predictability — you'll be the person Sales leadership leans on to turn data into accountability, process into pipeline, and comp plans into performance. What You'll Do Salesforce Data Ownership & Hygiene Own the Salesforce data layer for Sales: object model accuracy, field definitions, pipeline data integrity, and the hygiene processes that keep opportunity data trustworthy. Build and maintain SFDC reports for Sales — pipeline views, stage conversion, rep activity, attainment — serving as the primary Salesforce reporting resource for Sales leadership and frontline managers. Define and enforce data entry standards across the Sales org; build the accountability loops (process, tooling, or workflow) that sustain hygiene over time without manual correction. Partner with the GTM Systems Architect on SFDC configuration changes, flow updates, and object model evolution driven by Sales process needs. Serve as the Sales-side data partner to the GTM Insights & Analytics Manager, ensuring Salesforce objects and fields are correctly structured as upstream inputs to Snowflake and the BI layer. Forecasting & Pipeline Cadences Own the Sales forecast process operationally: run the weekly pipeline and forecast review cadence, partner with frontline managers to validate SFDC data (deals, close dates, eGPV, stage accuracy), and ensure action items are followed through. Prepare pipeline review materials — pulling from SFDC reports — that surface trends, risks, slippage, and coverage gaps by segment for Sales leadership discussion. Proactively flag forecast risks and data quality issues; escalate coverage shortfalls and drive cross-functional conversations when pipeline generation is off track. Partner with the GTM Insights & Analytics Manager on forecast accuracy improvement: they bring the BI modeling and historical analysis; you bring the SFDC data discipline and process accountability. Support GTM MBR and QBR cadences with consistent, SFDC-sourced reporting inputs and segment-level operational narrative. Sales Compensation Design & Administration Own end-to-end compensation administration for the Sales organization — plan documents, quota assignments, attainment tracking, payout calculations, approval processes and dispute resolution. Partner with the Head of Revenue Operations and Finance to support annual comp plan design, ensuring plans are aligned to GTM strategy, bookings goals, and crediting rules for both standard and non-standard deal structures. Maintain the compensation administration platform as the system of record, ensuring calculation accuracy, auditability, and clean data lineage from deal close to payout. Manage the full comp calendar — plan communication, quota letter distribution, mid-year adjustments, and commission statement delivery. Administer SPIFs and accelerators; track performance and report outcomes to Sales leadership and Finance. Build and maintain comp infrastructure that scales with headcount growth and plan complexity — modular, documented, and auditable. Sales Process & Deal Desk Operations Own the documentation and operationalization of Sales processes and methodology — ensuring consistent execution from prospecting through close. Partner with Sales leadership and Enablement to drive process adoption and accountability, with clear feedback loops on where breakdowns occur in the funnel. Own the deal desk process for standard and non-standard pricing: define the approval matrix, set and enforce SLAs, resolve bottlenecks, and ensure contract and implementation handoffs execute without friction. Identify process gaps and prioritize improvements in partnership with the GTM Systems Architect; translate Sales business requirements into system changes. Optimize the Marketing → Sales → Implementation → Customer Success handoff, reducing friction at each transition point. Operating Cadences & GTM Rhythm Own the weekly pipeline and forecast review end-to-end: preparation, facilitation, and follow-through. Track open headcount and hiring progress across the Sales org; flag capacity and coverage risks to RevOps and Sales leadership. Partner with Sales leadership on bookings planning — coordinating inputs from segment leads, validating against historical data, and stress-testing plan assumptions. Support segment performance reviews by preparing SFDC-sourced operational inputs; partner with GTM Insights for the analytical narrative layer. What You'll Have We're looking for a Salesforce-native Sales operator who combines system precision with process ownership — someone whose SFDC data is clean enough to trust, whose comp statements arrive on time and without errors, and whose forecast reviews actually improve rep behavior. Core Experience & Mindset 5–8 years in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or Business Operations in a B2B SaaS environment. Deep Salesforce ownership experience — object model design, data hygiene management, and SFDC as the system of record for Sales. Direct experience owning sales compensation administration — plan design support, attainment tracking, payout calculation, and dispute management. Proven ability to own a forecasting cadence: running the process, driving data discipline in CRM, and delivering reliable roll-ups to leadership. Comfortable building and maintaining SFDC reports and dashboards for Sales leadership and frontline managers. Working knowledge of how Salesforce data flows into downstream systems — sufficient to partner effectively with Analytics Engineering and GTM Insights without owning those layers. Familiarity with modern data stack tooling (Snowflake, dbt, Fivetran, or equivalent) is a plus. High ownership orientation — identifies what needs to be done and does it without being directed. Strong cross-functional communicator: fluent in a forecast review with a sales manager and a comp dispute conversation with Finance in the same week. title: Business Development Representative, Spanish Speaking
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>This position is 100% remote and will be based in Spain.<br><br>GitLab is looking for an enthusiastic and strategic Business Development Representative (BDR) to join our growing Sales team. As a BDR at GitLab, you get the opportunity to lead the initial outreach to targeted accounts working in conjunction with the Field and Digital Marketing teams as well as the Sales and Customer Success teams. In this role you'll leverage creative marketing and sales tactics to prospect and engage with multiple buyer personas and roles to introduce GitLab's AI-powered DevSecOps platform. You'll be responsible for generating qualified meetings and pipeline for GitLab's Sales organization.</p> <p>Our BDRs come from a diverse background. Many have worked in closing roles previously or managed teams.</p> <p>We have an extensive onboarding and training program at GitLab and you'll be provided with necessary DevOps and GitLab knowledge to fulfill your role.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Execute outbound prospecting initiatives to generate qualified meetings and pipeline in your assigned territory.</li> <li>Generate New Logo opportunities and Growth opportunities on existing customer accounts.</li> <li>Conduct high-level discovery conversations with target accounts to understand business needs, qualify opportunities, and create Sales Accepted Opportunities (SAOs).</li> <li>Meet or exceed monthly and quarterly BDR-sourced Sales Accepted Opportunity (SAO) targets (e.g., Stage 1 and Stage 3 opportunities) by consistently converting qualified prospects into opportunities.</li> <li>Research and prioritize target accounts using business and industry knowledge to identify key players, uncover compelling events, and develop tailored outreach strategies.</li> <li>Execute a multi-touch outreach cadence (call, email, social, etc.) to all prospects in your assigned territory using Outreach to maximize engagement and conversion rates.</li> <li>Manage, track, and accurately report all prospecting activities and pipeline in Salesforce to provide clear visibility into performance and forecast.</li> <li>Collaborate with Field, Corporate, and Digital Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success teams to build targeted account lists, campaigns, and call strategies. Attend regional marketing events to engage participants, generate leads, and drive qualified Sales Accepted Opportunities (SAOs).</li> <li>Document and continuously improve Business Development Representative processes in the GitLab handbook in partnership with your Business Development Manager. Mentor new BDR hires to help them ramp quickly and navigate key accounts.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Fluency in Spanish.</li> <li>Previous tech industry experience in an outbound sales development role is required.</li> <li>Positive and energetic phone skills, excellent listening skills, strong writing skills.</li> <li>Ability to prioritize tasks, manage a high volume of outreach, and consistently follow through on prospecting activities.</li> <li>Proven experience taking initiative, persisting through setbacks, and independently driving projects or activities through to successful outcomes.</li> <li>Alignment with our values and working in accordance with those values.</li> <li>Knowledge of business process, roles, and organizational structure.</li> <li>Proficiency in using Salesforce, Sales Navigator, and Outreach or similar prospecting and sequencing tools.</li> <li><span style="font-size: 10pt;">The ability to travel for events such as trainings, team offsites, customer meetings, etc.</span></li> <li>Proficiency in English, our company language, is required for effective communication.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>As part of GitLab's growing Sales team, you will work closely with the Field and Digital Marketing teams, as well as the Sales and Customer Success teams. Our BDRs come from diverse backgrounds, and we provide extensive onboarding and training so you have the DevOps and GitLab knowledge you need to succeed. You'll partner with Account Executives, working fully remote and distributed across multiple U.S. time zones, collaborating asynchronously through GitLab, video calls, and shared playbooks. This role provides a clear path for advancing to an Account Executive position within GitLab.</p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/#examples-of-select-underrepresented-groups">underrepresented groups</a> are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.</p> <hr> <p><strong>Country Hiring Guidelines: </strong>GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  </p> <p><strong>Privacy Policy: </strong>Please review our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Policy.</a> Your privacy is important to us.</p> <p>GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/people-policies/inc-usa/#equal-employment-opportunity-policy" target="_blank">GitLab’s EEO Policy</a> and <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/labor-and-employment-notices/#eeoc-us-equal-employment-opportunity-commission-notices" target="_blank">EEO is the Law</a>. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Subject Matter Expert (SME), you'll be the deepest technical voice in the field for one product group, helping customers make technical decisions on GitLab's most important opportunities, roughly the top 10% by size or complexity.</p> <p>Account Solutions Architects (Account SAs) will bring you into prioritized opportunities. The Account SA owns the opportunity; you own your product group's success within it. You'll work directly with Product and Engineering, bringing customer needs and field insights into roadmap discussions. You'll also help the wider Solutions Architecture team build expertise through reusable assets, enablement, and coaching.</p> <p>You'll specialize in one product group, not all four. In Security & Compliance, you'll focus on GitLab Ultimate, application security, Dependency Firewall, software supply chain security, compliance, and artificial intelligence (AI) governance. In Platform, you'll focus on GitLab Dedicated, self-managed deployments, bring your own model, and cloud and hybrid architecture. In Core DevSecOps, you'll focus on GitLab Premium, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), source code management, Orbit, Artifact Central, and migrations. DevSecOps brings development, security, and operations together across software delivery. In AI & Competitive, you'll focus on GitLab Duo Agent Platform, agentic workflows, AI-native development, competitive displacement including GitHub, and migrations.</p> <p>Your success will be measured by technical win rate and bookings on SME-engaged opportunities, product-category commit attainment and consumption growth in your region, and Proof of Value (PoV) conversion rate, evaluation cycle time, and time from technical win to production use. We'll also measure how often Account SAs reuse your assets, their confidence in handling your product group without escalation, and the quality and impact of your feedback to Product.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Act as the technical authority for your product group on prioritized opportunities, from discovery and architecture through trials and PoV evaluations.</li> <li>Lead technical deep dives, workshops, and executive briefings that connect product capabilities to business outcomes and explain how GitLab differs from competing solutions.</li> <li>Design and improve standardized PoV templates with clear, repeatable success criteria. Account SAs own the customer PoV; you'll contribute product-specific content and expertise while keeping the evaluation connected to the broader GitLab platform.</li> <li>Equip account teams for product launches with Product Management and Product Marketing. Build demos and talk tracks, and turn early customer wins into reference stories.</li> <li>Serve as the escalation point for Account SAs and Post-Sales Solutions Architects (Post-Sales SAs) on complex product questions, integrations, and objections.</li> <li>Hand off PoV success criteria and architecture decisions to the Post-Sales SA with the account team when an opportunity closes. Stay involved until the customer's first production workload uses the product, and support complex accounts when Post-Sales SAs bring you in to drive adoption and consumption.</li> <li>Bring structured field feedback, competitive insights, and customer requirements to Product Management and Engineering with the wider SME team. Help manage early-access and design-partner programs, and represent GitLab through customer events, conferences, industry working groups, and published content.</li> <li>Build reference architectures, demo environments, competitive battlecards, PoV playbooks, and enablement content so account teams can handle more opportunities without your direct involvement. Mentor Account SAs and contribute to GitLab's global SME community of practice.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Substantial experience in technical pre-sales, solutions architecture, consulting, or software engineering, with deep, hands-on expertise in one domain: application security testing, supply chain security, and compliance; scalable cloud and hybrid platforms; large CI/CD environments and source code migrations; or production AI-assisted development, working prototypes, and competitive evaluations.</li> <li>Practical expertise in agentic and AI-assisted development workflows across planning, coding, testing, security, and delivery, applied in a customer-facing, pre-sales context.</li> <li>Experience winning technical decisions on large, complex enterprise opportunities through structured Proof of Concept (PoC) or PoV evaluations with defined success criteria and executive sign-off.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with Git, CI/CD, containers, Kubernetes, and at least one major cloud provider.</li> <li>The ability to lead a whiteboard session with engineers and present the business case to executives in the same meeting.</li> <li>Strong written communication, including the ability to turn complex topics into clear playbooks that others use.</li> <li>Comfort working asynchronously across time zones with Sales, Product, and Engineering.</li> <li>Optional: public speaking, published technical content, open source contributions, or relevant certifications in Kubernetes, cloud architecture, or security.</li> </ul> <p>If you
