More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As Principal Product Manager, Orbit, you'll define the vision, strategy, and roadmap for GitLab's software lifecycle context graph. Orbit connects source code and software development lifecycle data into a structured map of systems, relationships, dependencies, and ownership. You'll help engineers, software leaders, and artificial intelligence (AI) agents understand how teams build software and how changes affect the systems around it.</p> <p>You'll shape Orbit from its underlying graph model and query experiences through customer value, pricing, packaging, launch, and adoption. This role combines technical product leadership with building a business around software lifecycle context. You'll balance foundational platform work with near-term customer needs, working directly with technical customers and senior Engineering and Design leaders.</p> <p>You'll join Anand Ahire's product organization and partner across Product, Engineering, Design, Product Marketing, Sales, Solutions Engineering, and Customer Success, including the teams building GitLab Duo and the broader AI-powered development, security, and operations (DevSecOps) platform.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Define Orbit's multi-year vision and roadmap across graph models and ontology, ingestion and indexing, query and retrieval, developer and agent interfaces, governance, and enterprise readiness. Shape how Orbit works across GitLab.com, Self-Managed, Dedicated, GitLab Duo Agent Platform, MCP-based external agents, APIs, and developer tooling.</li> <li>Turn complex platform opportunities into customer problems, measurable outcomes, and investment decisions. Use evidence to decide where to invest, iterate, partner, or stop.</li> <li>Partner with Engineering and Design on architecture and implementation tradeoffs across graph data models, indexing, query systems, application programming interfaces (APIs), Model Context Protocol (MCP), authorization, and scale.</li> <li>Use AI tools such as Claude Code and GitLab to investigate problems, explore code and data, prototype concepts, and create or review merge requests when that's the fastest way to learn.</li> <li>Lead discovery with developers, engineering leaders, platform teams, security teams, and technical executives to validate needs around dependencies, ownership, change impact, vulnerability exposure, pipeline health, and software delivery risk. Build repeatable feedback into roadmap decisions and help customers understand the value of connected graph context over disconnected searches or API calls.</li> <li>Define target customers, priority use cases, differentiated value, and the path to product-market fit. Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Pricing, and Finance on positioning, packaging, pricing, launch, adoption, and expansion.</li> <li>Develop business cases and track adoption, retention, usage, customer value, and revenue outcomes. Support executive briefings, analyst conversations, customer workshops, and field enablement.</li> <li>Align teams and executive leaders around clear recommendations and tradeoffs without relying on direct authority. Mentor other product managers, share practical frameworks, and represent GitLab's product vision in customer and industry conversations.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience owning complex technical products or platforms at Staff, Principal, or equivalent scope, with a track record of defining vision and roadmaps across multiple teams.</li> <li>Deep technical fluency in one or more relevant areas, such as developer tools, DevOps, software delivery, data platforms, distributed systems, knowledge graphs, search, APIs, AI infrastructure, or agentic systems.</li> <li>The ability to work credibly with engineers on architecture, data models, APIs, scale, reliability, and security.</li> <li>Business judgment and experience in market assessment, product strategy, pricing, packaging, business cases, or commercialization of technical products.</li> <li>Experience taking a product, platform, or category from early concept through launch, customer adoption, and iteration.</li> <li>A customer-first approach and the ability to build trusted relationships with technical practitioners, engineering leaders, architects, and executives.</li> <li>Clear written and verbal communication, with experience explaining complex ideas, influencing across functions, and resolving competing priorities in ambiguous work.</li> <li>Practical experience using AI tools in product work, including exploring code and data, prototyping workflows, and creating or reviewing merge requests. You take ownership, learn quickly, and move between strategy and implementation detail.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>In GitLab's Analytics organization, we focus on making Orbit's context available through GitLab experiences, developer tools, MCP, APIs, and the command-line interface (CLI).</p> <p>Our challenge is to turn complex, connected data into useful, trustworthy context for engineers and agents. You'll work with engineering and cross-functional partners who value technical rigor, clear product thinking, rapid learning, and direct customer contact. the Senior Manager of Application Security.</p> <h4><strong>What you'll do </strong></h4> <ul> <li>Conduct and lead security research projects across multiple functional areas.</li> <li>Identify novel, systemic, and chained vulnerabilities in GitLab, where individual weaknesses combine for outsized impact.</li> <li>Validate security vulnerabilities through hands-on testing, developing proof-of-concept exploits that demonstrate real-world attack scenarios.</li> <li>Assess emerging industry vulnerability classes against the GitLab codebase, and drive remediation of the class rather than the instance.</li> <li>Lead security research into GitLab's AI and agentic surfaces, and define the security requirements that engineering teams build against.</li> <li>Build and direct the tooling and automation that scales security research, including agent-assisted vulnerability discovery across our codebase.</li> <li>Research the security posture of open source tools and dependencies integrated with GitLab, report findings to their maintainers, and track mitigation following our <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/security/disclosure/">responsible disclosure guidelines</a>.</li> <li>Solve technical problems of the highest scope, complexity, and ambiguity.</li> <li>Help shape the team and sub-department roadmap.</li> <li>Lead the integration of security research results into the engineering and business functions that need to act on them.</li> <li>Teach, mentor, and advise other domain experts and individual contributors across several teams.</li> <li>Share knowledge and novel vulnerability types with the security community.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>10+ years of experience in security research, penetration testing, or offensive security roles</li> <li>Strong ability in discovering and exploiting vulnerabilities in large codebase and complex systems</li> <li>Proficiency in two or more of Ruby, Go, Python, TypeScript, or Rust. </li> <li>Ability to read and analyze code across multiple languages and codebases</li> <li>Strong knowledge of AI frameworks</li> <li>Strong understanding of AI attack vectors including prompt injection, agent manipulation, and workflow exploitation</li> <li>At ease in establishing and driving complex remediation initiatives involving cross-functional teams</li> <li>Excellent written recommendations</li> <li>Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with creative thinking about attack scenarios</li> <li><strong>Nice to Have: </strong>Published security research or conference security challenges facing GitLab and its customers to enable GitLab to be the most secure software factory platform on the market. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As a Professional Services Technical Architect at GitLab, you'll lead the technical direction of customer engagements from early scoping and discovery through delivery. You'll design high-level architectures and implementation plans for GitLab infrastructure and functionality, and you'll make sure deliverables align with customer requirements and the Statement of Work (SOW). You'll coordinate and guide implementation work across GitLab Professional Services and partner consultants, support customers deploying GitLab in cloud and on-premises environments using tools like Terraform, Ansible, and the GitLab Environment Toolkit, and perform migrations to GitLab using Congregate. You'll provide DevOps and DevSecOps consulting and best practices, contribute reusable collateral such as documentation, delivery kits, and training materials, and share product release updates to help the team deliver consistent outcomes. This role combines deep technical expertise with customer-facing leadership in GitLab's remote, asynchronous, and values-driven environment.</p> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li>Designing and delivering GitLab reference architecture implementations for both self-managed and cloud environments, using infrastructure as code practices.</li> <li>Leading source code management and CI/CD migrations to GitLab, including large-scale enterprise moves using Congregate.</li> <li>Building repeatable delivery kits, documentation, and enablement materials that help Professional Services and partners deploy and adopt GitLab best practices.</li> <li>Lead the full technical delivery lifecycle for GitLab Professional Services engagements, from early scoping and technical discovery through implementation and handoff.</li> <li>Produce high-level and detailed technical designs for GitLab infrastructure and functionality, ensuring deliverables align with customer requirements and expectations.</li> <li>Evaluate and communicate scalability and security considerations (including compliance constraints) in proposed GitLab reference architectures and implementation plans.</li> <li>Deploy and configure GitLab in customer environments, including on-premises and major cloud providers, using Terraform, Ansible, and the GitLab Environment Toolkit (GET) aligned to reference architectures.</li> <li>Plan and execute source system migrations to GitLab using Congregate, partnering closely with customer stakeholders to reduce risk, protect data integrity, and minimize downtime.</li> <li>Provide DevOps and DevSecOps consulting and best-practice guidance, including advising on internal frameworks such as the Delivery Governance Framework (DGF) and GitLab Flow.</li> <li>Coordinate and oversee implementation work across GitLab team members, partners, and customer points of contact (POCs), ensuring clear asynchronous communication and decision capture, effective execution, and high-quality outcomes.</li> <li>Mentor Professional Services and partner consultants by contributing documentation, delivery kits, and training materials, and by leading enablement sessions on how to deliver and position service offerings.</li> <li>Maintain and improve delivery automation assets with an emphasis on code cleanliness, maintainability, and appropriate unit/integration testing.</li> <li>Support scoping and Statement of Work (SOW) creation with Professional Services Engagement Managers, stay current on monthly GitLab releases, and help Regional Delivery Managers with technical vetting and staffing assessments while maintaining a 55% billable utilization.</li> <li>Review and provide input to Professional Services training materials and presentations.</li> <li>Develop case studies, presentations, design documentation, and best-practice methodologies.</li> <li>Work closely with customer project teams to ensure accurate task-level articulation of work required.</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li>Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to lead technical discussions with customers and partners and communicate risks/trade-offs clearly in an asynchronous environment.</li> <li>UK remote based role.</li> <li>Up to 50% travel at times.</li> <li>Demonstrated experience delivering two or more of the following consulting services: source code management migration, cloud architecture, DevOps engineering, or continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) consulting services.</li> <li>Enterprise software development experience, with the ability to translate requirements into clear technical designs and implementation plans.</li> <li>Progressive DevOps platform experience, including designing and implementing reliable, scalable systems with clear performance and security trade-offs.</li> <li>Hands-on experience deploying and managing infrastructure in cloud providers and on-premises environments, including using tools such as Terraform and Ansible.</li> <li>Ability to write clean, maintainable automation/integration code (e.g., Terraform modules, Ansible roles, scripts) and validate changes with appropriate testing and code review.</li> <li>Experience performing migrations to GitLab, including using Congregate or similar migration tooling.</li> <li>Working knowledge of data consistency and integrity concepts (e.g., ACID properties) and how they impact migration design and performance trade-offs.</li> <li>Strong problem-solving, decision-making, organizational, and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities with minimal supervision.</li> <li>Comfort working in a remote, asynchronous environment, using documented decisions (e.g., issues, proposals, and runbooks) to keep work unblocked across time zones while collaborating effectively across GitLab team members, partners, and customer stakeholders.</li> <li>Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or other advanced technical degree, or equivalent experience.              #LI-CM1</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Professional Services Technical Architect is part of GitLab's Professional Services organization. We partner with customers who are transitioning to GitLab, expanding how they use an existing GitLab installation, or planning complex upgrades to their infrastructure and processes. Our team brings a diverse set of skills across GitLab deployment, maintenance, and day-to-day usage, along with deep technical knowledge of adjacent tools and platforms. Working closely with Engagement Managers, partner consultants, and customer stakeholders, we focus on delivering high-quality outcomes, sharing best practices, and helping customers realize faster time to value from their GitLab investment. We operate in GitLab's remote, asynchronous environment and rely on clear documentation and transparent communication to collaborate effectively.</p> <p> </p> <p>This role models skills and behaviour aligned with GitLab Values and typically reports to the Regional Delivery Manager. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>Aa Senior Account Executive, you’ll be the primary connection between GitLab and our Commercial & Enterprise customers, working with organizations of up to 4,000 team members to help them adopt and expand the world’s most comprehensive AI-powered DevSecOps platform. You’ll own a broad book of business across a wide range of opportunity sizes, guiding small, fast-growing teams as well as more complex projects as they modernize their software delivery with GitLab. Reporting to an Area Sales Manager and partnering closely with business development, marketing, and technical teams, you’ll run the full sales process: shaping the customer’s journey, documenting buying criteria and processes, ensuring accurate pipeline based on evidence, and sharing root-cause insights on wins and losses. In your first year, you’ll focus on building trusted relationships, delivering meaningful business outcomes for customers, and being the voice of the customer internally by contributing ideas to our public issue tracker and improving our sales handbook.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Report to an Regional Sales Director and own a broad book of Commercial & Enterprise business, from new prospects to growing existing accounts.</li> <li value="2">Manage the full sales cycle for Commercial & Enterprise prospects, from discovery and solution alignment through negotiation and close.</li> <li value="3">Support GitLab for Commercial & Enterprise prospects by clearly articulating our DevSecOps value proposition and aligning it to customer business outcomes.</li> <li value="4">Analyze wins and losses, contribute to root cause analyses, and share lessons learned with account managers, marketing, and technical teams.</li> <li value="5">Document and maintain accurate buying criteria, buying processes, next steps, and owners to ensure a reliable, evidence-based pipeline.</li> <li value="6">Contribute to improving our sales handbook and processes by documenting best practices and opportunities for refinement.</li> <li value="7">Provide account leadership and direction across pre- and post-sales, partnering closely with technical teams and customer success.</li> <li value="8">Represent the voice of the customer by contributing product feedback and ideas to our public issue tracker.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Proven success in software sales, ideally in a Enterprise market context, managing a varied book of business.</li> <li value="2">Ability to guide customers through the full buying journey, including defining buying criteria, mapping buying processes, and driving clear next steps.</li> <li value="3">Effective communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate with business development, marketing, technical teams, and sales management.</li> <li value="4">Experience documenting and maintaining accurate pipeline data and account plans based on evidence rather than assumptions.</li> <li value="5">Skill in conducting and contributing to win/loss and root cause analyses, and sharing insights to improve team performance and processes.</li> <li value="6">Proficiency in negotiation, presenting to customer stakeholders, and leading commercial discussions to close opportunities.</li> <li value="7">Interest in GitLab, open source software, and preferably familiarity with Git, software development tools, or application lifecycle management.</li> <li value="8">Alignment with GitLab’s values and an interest in contributing from diverse or transferable sales backgrounds, with willingness to travel in line with company policy.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Commercial & Enterprise Sales team focuses on helping growing organizations adopt and expand GitLab’s AI-powered DevSecOps platform across their software delivery lifecycle. title: Senior AI Engineer
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As an Senior AI Engineer at GitLab, you'll help build the foundation for GitLab's transformation into an AI-first company. Reporting to the Director, Enterprise AI, you'll be a hands-on technical leader responsible for delivering internal AI-powered solutions that drive measurable business outcomes.</p> <p>Building fast matters, but it's not enough on its own. This role starts with understanding the real problem: mapping how work moves across teams, tools, and handoffs, identifying the true constraint, and validating whether AI is the right solution before you begin development. From there, you'll take ownership from discovery through deployment, combining strong engineering skills with systems thinking and business understanding.</p> <p>Your initial focus will span Sales, Marketing, and Customer Support, where you will embed AI solutions into key systems and workflows. This role offers the opportunity to shape how GitLab team members work, improve flow across the organization, and help advance our mission in a remote, asynchronous, and values-driven environment.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Diagnose business problems before building solutions. Map workflows, identify constraints, and confirm whether AI is the right intervention. Be prepared to say "this doesn't need AI" when that's the honest answer.</li> <li>Own AI initiatives end-to-end, from stakeholder discovery and technical design through implementation, deployment, and iteration.</li> <li>Design, develop, and ship AI-powered solutions quickly, delivering working prototypes in days, not months, with a focus on practical outcomes and measurable business value.</li> <li>Improve organizational flow by building solutions that reduce bottlenecks, shorten lead times, and increase throughput. Measure success using flow metrics alongside adoption and ROI.</li> <li>Integrate AI capabilities into existing systems and workflows using APIs, orchestration tools, and modern AI platforms, including GitLab Duo Agent Platform, where appropriate. The right tool wins, whether that's custom code, a platform, or a well-crafted prompt.</li> <li>Be Customer Zero: leverage and showcase GitLab's AI offerings wherever possible, feeding real-world usage insights back to R&D.</li> <li>Partner closely with stakeholders across functions to understand the real constraints. Ask the right questions, bridge technical and non-technical perspectives, and align on outcomes before jumping to solutions.</li> <li>Define and track success through business metrics, flow metrics, and feedback loops that make performance visible and actionable.</li> <li>Contribute to technical direction by evaluating tools, documenting patterns, and creating reusable foundations that help the team scale its impact.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>A Technologist at Heart - </strong>Genuinely invested in technology, the foundational and the cutting-edge in equal measure. You're as energised by a well-designed API integration as you are by the latest foundation model release. You reach for the simplest solution that solves the problem well, rather than forcing new technology when proven approaches would do. AI is a powerful part of your toolkit, but it sits on top of solid engineering fundamentals, not in place of them.</li> <li><strong>Competent, Confident Coding Skills - </strong>You can build working solutions end-to-end, write clean and maintainable code, and debug effectively. Whether your skills were honed in a traditional engineering role, through building automations, or shipping side projects, what matters is that you can deliver production-quality work independently.</li> <li><strong>AI</strong><strong> & LLM </strong><strong>Technical Depth - </strong>Strong proficiency in at least one modern scripting language (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or similar) and a solid understanding of REST APIs, GraphQL, and integration patterns. Deep, practical experience with modern AI technologies, specifically: Prompt engineering as a core discipline: designing effective system prompts, managing context windows, structuring multi-turn interactions, evaluating output quality, and iterating systematically on prompt design.</li> <li><strong>Model selection and cost-performance trade-offs: </strong>understanding when a smaller fine-tuned model outperforms a general-purpose large one, when RAG is the right architecture versus expanding the context window, and how to make principled decisions about capability versus cost.</li> <li><strong>Agentic architecture patterns: </strong>tool use, multi-agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop designs, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and production-grade reliability patterns.Practical fluency across the LLM ecosystem: hands-on experience with models from Anthropic, OpenAI, open-source alternatives, and the judgment to know which to reach for and when.</li> <li><strong>AI Safety & Risk Awareness - </strong>You think critically about how the solutions you build could be exploited, misused, or produce unintended consequences. You know how to design appropriate guardrails (input validation, output filtering, access controls, prompt injection defences, and data leakage prevention) and you treat these as first-class engineering concerns.</li> <li><strong>Systems Thinking & Diagnostic Rigour - </strong>The ability to look at a complex process and see the constraint. Comfortable mapping how work flows end-to-end, identifying bottlenecks, and tracing problems to root causes before proposing solutions. You instinctively ask "what's actually blocking flow here?" before asking "what model should I use?"</li> <li><strong>Business System Expertise - </strong>Familiarity with the landscape of enterprise business systems, CRM (Salesforce), marketing automation (Marketo), support platforms (Zendesk), integration and orchestration tools (Workato), AI platforms (Relevance AI), and enterprise search and knowledge tools (Glean). You don't need deep experience with all of these, but to understand what they do, how they fit together, and be willing to build with and across them. A strong understanding of enterprise data models and workflows is essential.</li> <li><strong>Broad Functional Understanding - </strong>Ability to have meaningful conversations with stakeholders across diverse domains and quickly understand their unique needs.</li> <li><strong>End-to-End Ownership - </strong>Track record of owning complex initiatives from discovery through delivery. Comfortable operating with ambiguity and driving to measurable outcomes independently.</li> <li><strong>Product Mindset - </strong>Ability to scope MVPs, prioritise ruthlessly, and deliver iteratively. In addition, consider adoption, user experience, and business outcomes.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Preferred requirements</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with GitLab platform and CI/CD workflows</li> <li>Background in consulting, solutions engineering, or customer-facing technical roles</li> <li>Familiarity with value stream mapping, flow metrics, or Theory of Constraints thinking</li> <li>Experience with low-code/no-code orchestration tools (n8n, Make, Workato) alongside custom development</li> <li>Previous startup or high-growth company experience</li> <li>Experience mentoring or leading technical projects with junior engineers</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>You will join the Enterprise Technology & AI team. We're the backbone of the organisation, driving transformation in how GitLab team members make decisions, operate at scale, and deliver results for our customers.</p> <p>We believe the best AI solutions start with understanding the system, not the technology. We value people who think in constraints and flow, who build with conviction, and who never stop learning. We work in an all-remote, asynchronous setting, guided by GitLab's values of collaboration, results, efficiency, diversity, inclusion and belonging, iteration, and transparency.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. Your impact in the first year will be measured by customer trust, reduced critical incidents, and clear, reusable support content that empowers customers and GitLab teams alike.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Provide technical support to our largest Self-managed, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab.com customers, ensuring their GitLab environments remain stable and performant.</li> <li value="2">Troubleshoot and resolve complex, critical, and sensitive support issues using tools like Zendesk, logs, and Linux utilities such as strace, through email and video conferencing.</li> <li value="3">Build strong, proactive relationships with key customer stakeholders, helping them prioritize and address their most important technical blockers.</li> <li value="4">Collaborate with <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/product/">Product</a>, <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/development/">Development</a>, <a Success</a>, and <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/sales/">Sales</a> teams to drive bug fixes, influence feature development, and help shape product goals and roadmap.</li> value="8">Contribute to team growth by participating in hiring processes, including reviewing applications and assessments and joining interviews.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Background managing complex, customer facing support cases end to end, from initial inquiry and triage through reproduction, escalation, and resolution.</li> <li value="2">Advanced troubleshooting skills with the ability to investigate ambiguous, multi-layered technical issues and identify root causes across applications, infrastructure, and integrations.</li> <li value="3">Strong Linux systems administration knowledge (LFCE or RHCE equivalent), including performance analysis and low-level debugging tools.</li> <li value="4">Practical experience with GitLab and continuous integration / continuous delivery (CI/CD), including how different deployment models and outages affect customers.</li> <li value="5">Ability to write and maintain clear, reusable support content such as knowledge articles, runbooks, and troubleshooting guides.</li> <li value="6">Proficiency with scripting languages (such as Ruby or Bash) and familiarity with model-view-controller (MVC) frameworks, preferably Ruby on Rails.</li> <li value="7">Effective communication skills for explaining complex technical topics to audiences with varying technical backgrounds and for building rapport with customer stakeholders.</li> <li value="8">Familiarity with DevOps practices and technologies such as Kubernetes and serverless platforms, with openness to applying transferable skills from related domains.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Support team is a fully distributed, global group across the AMER, EMEA, and APAC regions, focused on helping customers get the most Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As an Assigned Support Engineer, you’ll be a trusted technical advisor to GitLab’s largest Self-managed, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab.com customers, helping them avoid operational disruption and get the most from GitLab. You’ll combine deep Linux systems expertise, GitLab and CI/CD knowledge, and a proactive support mindset to understand each customer’s environment, anticipate and prevent issues, and solve complex technical and business challenges. In a typical week, you might be prioritizing strategic blockers with customer stakeholders, partnering with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales to drive defect resolution and influence the roadmap, or diving into code, logs, and tools like strace to troubleshoot performance issues. Your impact in the first year will be measured by customer trust, reduced critical incidents, and clear, reusable support content that empowers customers and GitLab teams alike.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Provide technical support to our largest Self-managed, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab.com customers, ensuring their GitLab environments remain stable and performant.</li> <li value="2">Troubleshoot and resolve complex, critical, and sensitive support issues using tools like Zendesk, logs, and Linux utilities such as strace, through email and video conferencing.</li> <li value="3">Build strong, proactive relationships with key customer stakeholders, helping them prioritize and address their most important technical blockers.</li> <li value="4">Collaborate with <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/product/">Product</a>, <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/development/">Development</a>, <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/infrastructure/">Infrastructure</a>, <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-success/">Customer Success</a>, and <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/sales/">Sales</a> teams to drive bug fixes, influence feature development, and help shape product goals and roadmap.</li> <li value="5">Act as a technical expert on GitLab and CI/CD implementations, advising customers on how incidents and service interruptions impact their workflows and how to mitigate them.</li> <li value="6">Create and improve support content, including documentation and knowledge articles, to help customers and GitLab team members resolve issues more efficiently.</li> <li value="7">Partner closely with Support Engineering team members through <a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/support-pairing/?_gl=1%2a1vj7usl%2a_ga%2aMTYyOTI0OTAxNC4xNjc4NzIwMDg0%2a_ga_ENFH3X7M5Y%2aMTY4NDgzNDU0OC4xMTAuMS4xNjg0ODM2NDM3LjAuMC4w">pairing sessions</a> and <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/support/#support-stable-counterpart">stable counterpart</a> relationships to share knowledge and solve problems together.</li> <li value="8">Contribute to team growth by participating in hiring processes, including reviewing applications and assessments and joining interviews.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Background managing complex, customer facing support cases end to end, from initial inquiry and triage through reproduction, escalation, and resolution.</li> <li value="2">Advanced troubleshooting skills with the ability to investigate ambiguous, multi-layered technical issues and identify root causes across applications, infrastructure, and integrations.</li> <li value="3">Strong Linux systems administration knowledge (LFCE or RHCE equivalent), including performance analysis and low-level debugging tools.</li> <li value="4">Practical experience with GitLab and continuous integration / continuous delivery (CI/CD), including how different deployment models and outages affect customers.</li> <li value="5">Ability to write and maintain clear, reusable support content such as knowledge articles, runbooks, and troubleshooting guides.</li> <li value="6">Proficiency with scripting languages (such as Ruby or Bash) and familiarity with model-view-controller (MVC) frameworks, preferably Ruby on Rails.</li> <li value="7">Effective communication skills for explaining complex technical topics to audiences with varying technical backgrounds and for building rapport with customer stakeholders.</li> <li value="8">Familiarity with DevOps practices and technologies such as Kubernetes and serverless platforms, with openness to applying transferable skills from related domains.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Support team is a fully distributed, global group across the AMER, EMEA, and APAC regions, focused on helping customers get the most from GitLab by troubleshooting complex issues and digging into code and logs to understand why something is not working as expected. As an Assigned Support Engineer, you’ll be part of our broader Support Engineering organization, working closely with other Support Engineers through regular pairing sessions, 1:1s, coffee chats, and Slack conversations to stay connected while collaborating asynchronously across time zones. We balance autonomy with accountability, giving you flexibility to structure your shift in a way that fits your life while ensuring we can reliably address customer issues. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.</p> <hr> <p><strong>Country Hiring Guidelines: </strong>GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Senior Backend Engineer on the Duo Chat team, focused on Chat Engine, you'll build the core AI capabilities behind GitLab Duo Chat, the natural-language and agentic interface to the GitLab DevSecOps platform. Much of your work will involve building flow components and agentic flows in the Flow Registry, the Python framework built on LangGraph within our Duo Workflow Service that powers agentic chat, and integrating them with the GitLab Rails monolith.</p> <p>You'll own complex backend features from start to finish across both services. You'll integrate large language models and orchestrate multi-agent flows so customers can work faster and more securely across the software development lifecycle. This work sits where GitLab's core platform meets its AI strategy, and reliability, performance, and answer quality directly shape the customer experience.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Design and build flow components and agentic flows in the Flow Registry using Python and LangGraph within the Duo Workflow Service. These reusable building blocks power agentic Duo Chat and, increasingly, other AI features across GitLab.</li> <li>Develop, ship, and maintain backend features for GitLab Duo Chat across the Python Duo Workflow Service and the GitLab Rails monolith in a secure, well-tested, and performant way.</li> <li>Integrate new generative AI models, providers, tools, and multi-agent orchestration patterns into Duo Chat to expand its capabilities and improve answer quality.</li> <li>Design, implement, and review GraphQL and Representational State Transfer (REST) application programming interfaces (APIs) and related monolith logic, including chat entry points, permissions, and foundational-flow registration. Keep contracts with frontend clients and host systems reliable and clear.</li> <li>Improve debugging, observability, and test coverage using pytest, RSpec, and related frameworks; track and improve latency, error rates, and test coverage so AI-powered chat workflows stay reliable at scale.</li> <li>Collaborate with Product, User Experience (UX), frontend, and AI specialists to refine requirements and deliver high-quality improvements through iteration.</li> <li>Document standards, patterns, and learnings with other engineers, raising the bar for safe AI integration and evidence-driven engineering.</li> <li>Participate in Tier 2 on-call rotations to troubleshoot production issues, contribute to root cause analysis, and strengthen resiliency.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Significant experience building and maintaining production Python backends, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous or long-running workloads.</li> <li>Practical experience designing and shipping AI-powered, agentic backend features, including large language model integration, tool or function calling, and multi-agent orchestration. You use sound judgment about large language model limitations and safe use in production.</li> <li>Working proficiency in Ruby on Rails, or a strong willingness to learn it. Duo Chat integrates deeply with the GitLab monolith for chat entry points, GraphQL, permissions, and flow registration, and most of GitLab's codebase is written in Ruby.</li> <li>Proficiency designing or extending REST or GraphQL APIs with attention to scalability, maintainability, and backward compatibility.</li> <li>Strong Structured Query Language (SQL) skills and familiarity with relational databases such as PostgreSQL, including efficient queries and data modeling.</li> <li>Ability to find, diagnose, and prevent performance and reliability problems at scale.</li> <li>Experience solving technical problems of high scope and complexity and advocating for quality, security, and performance improvements across your team.</li> <li>Openness to learning and collaborating in an async-first, distributed team, applying transferable skills from related technologies or domains. Hands-on experience with agent frameworks such as LangGraph or LangChain is a strong plus.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>We're part of GitLab's AI Engineering organization and own the AI-powered chat experience embedded across the GitLab platform. Chat Engine is the backend-focused team within the Duo Chat group.</p> <p>We're backend, frontend, and AI specialists working asynchronously across time zones, using issues, merge requests, and documentation as our main collaboration tools. Our focus is to expand generative and agentic AI capabilities, improve the performance and reliability of chat workflows, and strengthen the debugging and testing foundations that let us run AI features safely at scale.</p> <p>For more on how we work, see the <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/ai/duo-chat/">team handbook</a> page.</p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. title: Senior Backend Engineer, Architecture Engineering: Nonlinear Productivity
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Senior Backend Engineer on GitLab's Nonlinear Productivity team, you'll find and remove friction across the software development lifecycle using reliable AI-powered automation — diagnosing problems like long review cycles, manual release steps, and brittle automation, then building the automation and process changes that resolve them for good.</p> <p>Some examples of the problems this team takes on:</p> <ul> <li>Cutting the time it takes to complete a good code review — one that still keeps a human in the loop — by half, using agentic solutions.</li> <li>Turning a manual, error-prone release step into an agentic workflow that catches its own mistakes before a human ever has to.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Identify sources of friction across GitLab's software development lifecycle and scope agentic solutions to address them, turning vague pain points into concrete, buildable proposals.</li> <li>Design and build reliable AI-powered systems that follow step-by-step workflows, use tools and safety checks, and correct errors before taking engineering action — the kind of output you can actually trust with real engineering decisions.</li> <li>Build and maintain evaluation tools that judge agent output on correctness, constraint compliance, and cost, not on whether it merely "seems to work."</li> <li>Work across GitLab's codebase as each problem requires, going wherever the friction actually is rather than staying inside one service or product area.</li> <li>Apply distributed systems judgment to identify generated code that may fail under concurrency, at scale, or across self-managed, dedicated, and multi-tenant deployments, catching failures before they reach customers.</li> <li>Collaborate with the India-based group, sharing roadmaps, findings, and reusable agent tooling</li> <li>Take ownership of a greenfield problem space from day one, helping shape a proven internal fix into a capability GitLab could offer customers externally, with your scope and impact free to grow as the team scales.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Hands-on experience building agentic or large language model-based systems — multi-step orchestration, tool use, guardrails, and recovery patterns — and making them reliable in production, not treated as one-off prompts or demonstrations.</li> <li>A track record of working autonomously in unfamiliar codebases, getting oriented quickly, and driving solutions through completion.</li> <li>Strong distributed systems knowledge, including coordination, consistency, idempotency, rate limiting, failure modes, and degradation under load.</li> <li>Proficiency in Go, Rust, or Python, in that order of team priority, and the ability to read and modify code in the other languages.</li> <li>Helpful experience includes shipping autonomous agents that complete real tasks from start to finish; improving build systems, release processes, review workflows, or other parts of the software development lifecycle; and working with globally distributed teams, large language model workload costs, or production constraints across on-premises, air-gapped, single-tenant, and software-as-a-service deployments.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Nonlinear Productivity — shortened internally to "NLP," with no relation to natural language processing — is one of GitLab's newest teams: a strategic incubation group that reports into AI Platform leadership under the direct sponsorship of the CTO. It's split into a US group (this role) and an India-based group working the same charter; the two sync on roadmap and tooling a few times a week but otherwise run day to day on their own. title: Senior Backend Engineer, Database Excellence (Ruby)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As a Senior Backend Engineer with the <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/">Database Excellence group</a>, you'll build and evolve the data frameworks and tooling that keep GitLab's application datastores scalable, healthy, and safe across both GitLab.com and thousands of self-managed instances. A primary focus for this role is building proactive data growth controls for GitLab.com, including retention and lifecycle management frameworks, enforcement of retention policies at schema-change time, and tooling that keeps database growth sustainable as AI-driven development accelerates how quickly data accumulates. You'll help teams across GitLab reason confidently about data architecture, placement, and lifecycle management, while proactively identifying saturation points in our GitLab.com infrastructure and driving corrective actions with partner teams. With the team's recent move into the Data Engineering organization, you'll also shape new scalability and data health features for self-managed customers, working hands-on with PostgreSQL and Ruby on Rails in a fully remote, highly collaborative environment.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li value="1"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/22105">Data Growth Controls (retention enforcement and data lifecycle management)</a></li> <li value="2"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/epics/17719"><u><span class="textUnderline">SQL Traffic Replay Tooling</span></u></a></li> <li value="3"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/epics/16152"><u><span class="textUnderline">Background Operations Framework</span></u></a></li> </ul> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Develop and iterate backend features and data frameworks that make it safe and efficient for GitLab teams to work with data at scale across SaaS and self-managed deployments.</li> <li value="2">Design and build data retention and lifecycle management frameworks, including retention policy enforcement, bulk data removal tooling, and automated identification of tables that need retention policies.</li> <li value="3">Build shift-left guardrails, such as static analysis checks and schema-change-time enforcement, that catch unsustainable data growth patterns before they reach production.</li> <li value="4">Collaborate closely with product management, UX, frontend, infrastructure, software delivery, and analytics teams to design and ship high-performing solutions</li> <li value="5">Review and improve database-related changes from other engineers and community contributors, ensuring data integrity, safety, and performance across all deployment scenarios.</li> <li value="6">Design, build, and maintain tooling such as SQL traffic replay and background operations frameworks to proactively surface and address scalability and performance issues.</li> <li value="7">Research, design, and implement improvements to data retention and lifecycle management, database performance, scalability, and data health, including areas like soft delete strategies and database migration testing.</li> <li value="8">Document database best practices, patterns to avoid, and data architecture guidance to enable developers to make informed decisions.</li> <li value="9">Develop proactive tooling and guardrails that help developers detect and remediate potential performance and data issues early in the development lifecycle.</li> <li value="10"> </li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Professional software engineering experience working with PostgreSQL in large, complex production environments, including high availability solutions with automatic failover and zero-downtime data migrations as well as managing large or fast-growing datasets through approaches such as data retention, archiving, partitioning, or lifecycle management.</li> <li value="2">Proficiency with Ruby on Rails or another Ruby framework, including designing, implementing, and reviewing backend features.</li> <li value="3">Ability to reason about software design, algorithms, and performance trade-offs at a system level.</li> <li value="4">Strong written communication skills and comfort working asynchronously in an all-remote, distributed team.</li> <li value="5">Self-directed work style with effective organizational skills and the ability to manage priorities as a "manager of one".</li> <li value="6">Alignment with GitLab's values, including transparency, collaboration, inclusion, and contribution to open source.</li> <li value="7">Openness to learning and applying new tools and approaches, including transferable experience from related data, infrastructure, or developer tooling domains.</li> <li value="8">Willingness to participate in our <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/#tier-2-on-call">tier 2 dabase on-call rotation</a> in your time zone.</li> </ul> <p>The <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/">Database Excellence Group</a> is a remote, agile backend team that builds and maintains the frameworks, patterns, and tooling that enable GitLab teams to work confidently with data at scale across all application datastores. You'll be a technical anchor for the team, driving the evolution of platform readiness from manual, ad-hoc assessments toward intelligent, agentic automation. <p>You'll receive onboarding and technical guidance from other engineers and team leadership as you establish the technical direction for the Platform Readiness team.</p> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Contribute to the Platform Readiness team's agentic workflows</strong> on the Duo Agent Platform: design, implement, and evolve the Core Agentic Workflow (currently published to the AI Catalog as a DAP flow) and the Requirements Agent, enabling automated evaluation of platform readiness assessments against platform requirements</li> <li><strong>Evolve the platform requirements knowledge base</strong>: contribute to schema design, validation tooling, and CI systems that power the agentic workflow; ensure the schema captures the full scope of platform readiness concerns requirements, domain skills, and validation logic without requiring specific domain knowledge</li> <li><strong>Contribute to the quality control feedback loop</strong>: design systems that surface assessment errors, missed gaps, and content drift back to the governance loop for continuous improvement; measure and improve assessment accuracy and guidance relevance</li> <li><strong>Mentor other engineers</strong> on the team in agentic-workflow standards, prompt discipline, evaluation methodology, and the principles of human-AI collaboration in platform readiness</li> <li><strong>Contribute to technical documentation and architectural decision records</strong> that document the Platform Readiness team's technical evolution and rationale for key design choices</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <h3>Required Experience & Skills</h3> <ul> <li><strong>5+ years of software engineering experience</strong> with at least 2+ years in backend, platform, or developer-facing tooling</li> <li><strong>Strong proficiency in TypeScript/Node, Python, or Golang</strong> (Ruby a plus)</li> <li><strong>Experience shipping developer-facing tooling</strong> where the primary user is another engineer</li> <li><strong>Understanding of GitLab-style development workflows</strong> (issues, epics, merge requests, CI/CD, code review) as first-class artifacts that automation can read and reason about</li> <li><strong>Ability to work in cross-functional environments</strong> across multiple platform teams</li> <li><strong>Experience with structured content systems, schemas, or validation tooling</strong></li> </ul> <h3>Highly Valued Experience</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Experience with AI/agentic systems</strong> (DAP, ADK, LangGraph, or similar) OR demonstrated ability to reason rigorously about the boundary between what AI should decide and what humans must own</li> <li><strong>Experience integrating with LLM APIs</strong> and reasoning about cost, latency, evaluation, and failure modes</li> <li><strong>Background in developer experience or platform engineering</strong></li> <li><strong>Experience with governance patterns</strong> for shared standards and cross-org decision-making</li> <li><strong>Open source contribution history</strong> in platform, developer experience, or AI infrastructure</li> <li><strong>PostgreSQL or other relational database experience</strong> at scale</li> </ul> <h3>What Makes You Stand Out (Strong Plus)</h3> <ul> <li>You've <strong>shipped agentic workflows in production</strong> and dealt with the operational complexities of AI-driven automation</li> <li>You have <strong>experience designing schema-driven content systems</strong> with non-engineer authors and evolving them as requirements change</li> <li>You've <strong>built developer platform teams at scale</strong> and understand the dynamics of enabling other engineers</li> <li>You have <strong>observability and monitoring experience for AI systems</strong>, including evaluation metrics, cost tracking, and failure analysis</li> <li>You can <strong>explain complex concepts</strong> (agentic workflows, platform readiness, governance) clearly to platform teams, feature teams, product managers, and executives</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Platform Readiness team is part of GitLab Developer Experience, building internal developer tooling capability for platform readiness across GitLab's four deployment targets: Self-Managed, Dedicated, Dedicated for Government, and GitLab.com. We partner with platform teams, feature teams, and product management to ensure every feature is evaluated against platform readiness requirements before it ships.</p> <p><strong>Current challenges we're tackling:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Moving from manual coordination to embedded automation:</strong> Transitioning from manual, ad-hoc platform readiness assessments to automated, agentic evaluation while maintaining human oversight and trust</li> <li><strong>Building a structured, machine-readable requirements body:</strong> Evolving the platform requirements schema to capture the full scope of platform readiness concerns across all domains and platforms</li> <li><strong>Making platform readiness native to the tools feature teams already use:</strong> Enabling platform teams to contribute domain expertise and validation logic without requiring deep Platform Readiness infrastructure knowledge</li> <li><strong>Building the measurement systems to know we're working:</strong> Creating observability and evaluation frameworks that give us confidence in agentic-workflow decisions and surface failures early</li> </ul> <p><strong>Team structure:</strong></p> <p>You'll be joining a newly established Platform Readiness team that is building the capability to embed platform readiness intelligence into the development lifecycle. As a Senior engineer, you'll work closely with team leadership to define technical direction while mentoring other engineers on the team. title: Senior Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>The Trusted Agentic Development team sits within GitLab's Developer Experience group and builds the platforms our engineers rely on every day. GitLab engineers increasingly build software with artificial intelligence agents. Agents can generate code and tests in seconds, but they can also produce passing test suites for software that doesn't work as intended. As a Senior Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development, you'll own the technical thesis for closing that validation gap and build the early proof yourself. You'll rethink what validation means when the author is an agent and make the feedback loop fast, automatic, and trustworthy enough that teams choose to adopt it.</p> <ul> <li value="1">Validation that confirms agent-generated code does what was intended, so a passing suite means a working feature and not just a satisfied proxy.</li> <li value="2">Mid-loop feedback that helps an agent self-correct toward working software instead of green assertions.</li> <li value="3">Language-aware approaches under one shared model of what "trusted" means, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, while allowing the right technique to differ by language.</li> <li value="4">Real measurement of whether engineers trust and adopt the path, fed straight back into the platform.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Own the technical thesis for how GitLab validates software when an agent is the author, and turn it into an architecture the team can build against.</li> <li value="2">Prototype the hard parts by building early versions of feedback mechanisms that catch the gap between passing tests and working software, proving what works before the team scales it.</li> <li value="3">Develop approaches for GitLab's primary stacks, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, under one shared definition of "trusted," while allowing the right technique to differ by language.</li> <li value="4">Design the mid-loop feedback an agent needs to self-correct toward working software rather than green assertions, and build the systems that deliver it.</li> <li value="5">Collaborate with engineering teams to adopt these approaches, measure adoption, engineer trust, and validation quality, and use those findings to improve the platform.</li> <li value="6">Set technical direction the team can build on, review designs, and help teammates grow their technical judgment.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Deep, current, hands-on experience building real software with artificial intelligence agents, ideally across more than one language, and a clear understanding of why agent output can pass tests yet fail in production.</li> <li value="2">A strong point of view on the validation gap and concrete ideas for closing it, backed by approaches you've built or tried.</li> <li value="3">Experience designing distributed systems designed to run on Kubernetes first.</li> <li value="3">The technical range to design systems rather than tune a single framework, and the judgment to know when a solution should be general or language-specific.</li> <li value="4">You prototype to learn, and you ship.</li> <li value="5">The ability to influence engineers across an organization without formal authority through working code and sound reasoning.</li> <li value="6">Strong written communication in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.</li> <li value="7">Alignment with GitLab's values, especially collaboration, iteration, and transparency.</li> </ul> <p>This isn't a quality assurance or test automation role. We aren't looking for depth in a particular testing framework. We're looking for someone who has built with agents, experienced the validation gap firsthand, and wants to solve it.</p> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Trusted Agentic Development team is part of GitLab's Developer Experience group. This is a software engineering role, not ticket-taking internal IT, AI evangelism disconnected from shipped code, or customer-billable Professional Services delivery.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Use Claude Code, GitLab Duo, and other coding agents as your primary development environment for planning, implementation, refactoring, testing, reviews, and documentation. Run multiple agents in parallel on well-scoped tasks, critically review their output, and own every line that reaches production.</li> <li>Build and maintain the team's agent harness, including shared AGENTS.md conventions, skills, slash commands, hooks, subagent definitions, and continuous integration checks. Measure and share what works, publish reusable patterns, and retire those that don't.</li> <li>Ship agents and multi-step workflows for account research, success planning, scoping, status reporting, and customer onboarding. Package them as skills and plugins for non-engineers using Claude, Claude in Slack, and GitLab Duo Agent Platform.</li> <li>Build MCP servers and connectors for governed access to GitLab, Salesforce, Gainsight, Kantata, Thought Industries, Gong, Snowflake, and other enterprise systems. Add evaluations, tracing, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints to keep internal and customer-facing agents measurable, auditable, and safe with customer data.</li> <li>Evolve the CX Application Platform's gateway, Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure, including Elastic Container Service (ECS), Relational Database Service (RDS), and Lambda, Terraform configuration, application scaffold, and deployment path. Own applications such as PS Compass, Congregate, and GitLab University and its integrations, documenting build-versus-buy and consolidate-or-sunset decisions.</li> <li>Ship production-quality Python and TypeScript through GitLab continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), with tests, observability, security review, and runbooks. Design every application for handoff, with documentation, monitoring, and shared ownership.</li> <li>Prototype with Customer Success, Digital Success, Professional Services, Education Services, and Training in days, not quarters. Help CX team members bring their own applications to production, and turn field learning into reusable reference implementations, development paths, and enablement.</li> <li>Contribute upstream to GitLab and share product feedback with Product and Engineering. Mentor engineers and non-engineers on agentic development and raise the team's code review bar.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience building and operating production software, owning multi-quarter work from ambiguity to production, choosing reusable platform solutions over one-off customization where appropriate, and designing for handoff.</li> <li>Daily, hands-on use of coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitLab Duo, or similar on production work. You can show how they've changed what you ship and how you maintain quality.</li> <li>Experience building with large language models (LLMs) beyond chat, including tool use, MCP servers, agent loops, context and retrieval design, prompt and workflow design, and evaluations.</li> <li>Strong Python skills with FastAPI or Flask and TypeScript skills with Vue or React, including application programming interface (API) design, authentication, authorization, and secure handling of customer and business data.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with AWS ECS, RDS, and Lambda, Terraform, Docker, and applications running behind single sign-on (SSO), such as Okta.</li> <li>Experience integrating enterprise systems through Representational State Transfer (REST) and GraphQL APIs, and fluency with Git, merge requests, and CI/CD.</li> <li>Experience translating non-engineering stakeholders' workflows into technical plans and writing clear asynchronous design documents, decision records, and enablement materials. You align with GitLab's values and are willing to use GitLab for your own work.</li> <li>Optional experience includes agent harness customization; the GitLab Development Kit, Duo Agent Platform custom agents and flows, or AI Catalog publishing; enterprise agent governance and data controls; customer success, professional services, or learning platforms such as Salesforce, Gainsight, Kantata, or Thought Industries; professional services economics and customer success metrics; Snowflake or similar warehouses; and technical writing, talks, or open source contributions on agentic development.</li> </ul> <p>We welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; you don't need to meet every nice-to-have to apply.</p> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>CX Platform Engineering builds and runs CX Applications for Customer Success, Digital Success, Professional Services, Education Services, and Training. We own the CX Application Platform's gateway and infrastructure alongside our application portfolio: GitLab University, the Foundational Onboarding Agent in GitLab Duo Agent Platform, Congregate, PS Compass, and Customer Wins. We build the first version with the people doing the work, turn what we learn into a reusable pattern, then hand it off so it runs without us. We reward leverage, not heroics, and don't leave tools dependent on one person.</p> <h4><br><br></h4><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps.
