Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h3><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h3> <p>As the Senior Director, Global Subject Matter Expertise (SME) Solutions Architecture, you will build and lead GitLab's Subject Matter Expert organization: three regional teams in AMER, EMEA and APJ, each covering Security & Compliance, Platform, Core DevSecOps, and AI & Competitive. This team is the depth layer of GitLab's technical selling model. It wins the most complex opportunities, scales product expertise into the Account SA team, and turns field insight into product direction.</p> <p>This is a leader of leaders role. You will manage three regional SME Managers, not individual contributors, and develop them as leaders in their own right. The SME organization is new, so we are looking for a transformational leader who thrives in ambiguity, builds structure where none exists, and has a track record of standing up high-performing technical teams in fast-growing, evolving businesses.</p> <p>You will work as a peer to GitLab's regional Solutions Architecture Senior Directors and partner closely with Sales, Customer Success, Product, Engineering, Product Marketing and Sales Operations. Together you will make sure GitLab brings the right depth to the right opportunities, and that what the field learns shapes what GitLab builds next.</p> <h3><strong>What you'll do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Set the strategy, operating model and global standards for the SME organization, aligned to the VP Global SA and GitLab's go-to-market plan.</li> <li>Build the resourcing model from product-level bookings and consumption targets. Size each product group by region based on where the plan needs specialist coverage.</li> <li>Act as the field's senior partner to Product Management and Engineering. Run a structured feedback loop that shapes roadmap, launch readiness and early-access programs.</li> <li>Hire, mentor and develop regional SME Managers and, through them, the full global team.</li> <li>Own the engagement model with the regional SA Senior Directors, Post-Sales SAs and Customer Success: triage rules, coverage thresholds, the closed-won handoff to Post-Sales SAs, and escalation paths.</li> <li>Create and improve upon the processes, metrics and KPIs for SME-led technical evaluations, workshops, demos and Proofs of Value.</li> <li>Partner with CRO staff, regional sales leaders and AVPs on product-category performance, forecast risk and competitive strategy.</li> <li>Partner with Enablement to drive  field readiness for new product launches with Product Marketing and Enablement, including Duo Agent Platform, security and platform offerings.</li> <li>Build strong relationships with key customers at the technical sponsor and executive level.</li> <li>Use AI to change how the team works, including deal research, demo creation, PoV automation and knowledge sharing.</li> <li>Drive organizational transformation by finding gaps early, building structure where none exists, and leading change without waiting for top-down direction.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>5+ years second-line leadership experience (managing managers) in Solutions Architecture, Sales Engineering or a technical specialist organization.</li> <li>Experience building or scaling a specialist, overlay or global SA team in enterprise SaaS, DevSecOps, security or developer tools.</li> <li>A record of tying technical-team design to bookings and consumption outcomes, with the data to show it.</li> <li>The ability to lead through ambiguity and rapid organizational change, bringing clarity and direction while strategy is still forming.</li> <li>Strong relationships with Product and Engineering leaders, and a history of shaping roadmap from field insight.</li> <li>Fluency across the software development lifecycle, application security (SAST, DAST, SCA), cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure), Kubernetes and AI-assisted development, including LLM evaluation and production deployment patterns.</li> <li>Executive presence with technical practitioners, managers and C-level stakeholders.</li> <li>Proven ability to partner across Sales, Partners, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Customer Success and Professional Services.</li> <li>A self-starting, entrepreneurial approach. You don't wait for a playbook; you write it.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>How you'll be measured</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Global product-category commit attainment and consumption growth.</li> <li>Time from technical win to first workload in customer’s production environment on SME-engaged opportunities compared with non-engaged opportunities.</li> <li>SME coverage and engagement speed on the top 10% of opportunities.</li> <li>Account Team capability lift: fewer escalations and more deals handled without an SME over time.</li> <li>Product impact: field sentiment on the product feedback process along with field-sourced requirements adopted into the roadmap.</li> <li>Team health: hiring against plan, manager development, engagement and retention.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>The Subject Matter Expertise (SME) organization is part of GitLab's Solutions Architecture team, a trusted technical partner for the field. SMEs bring the deepest product expertise to GitLab's most complex opportunities and carry customer feedback into conversations about product direction, enablement and value messaging. The team is distributed and all-remote, and relies on clear communication, strong judgment and shared operating practices across regions.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. metrics, accurately forecasting services bookings, and tracking key performance indicators related to bookings, margin, and attachment to strategic opportunities.</li> <li>Own the engagement lifecycle from initial discovery and pre-sales solutioning through scoping, SOW development, staffing alignment, and transition to delivery, ensuring engagements are deliverable, clearly defined, and outcome-oriented.</li> <li>Influence cross-functional teams by articulating GitLab’s professional services value proposition in the context of federal requirements and compliance frameworks, and by continuous improvement by training field teams on how to position and sell professional services by sharing trends, feedback, and suggestions that improve go-to-market content and operational processes.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Demonstrated progressive experience structuring, scoping, and selling professional services engagements in the region</li> to mission objectives and measurable business outcomes.</li> <li>Effective communication and interpersonal skills with executive presence, able to build trusted advisor relationships with division complex opportunities while maintaining accurate forecasting and consistent alignment with GitLab values and goals.</li> </ul> <p>The Professional Services Engagement Management team at GitLab is As artificial intelligence agents increasingly write and manage code alongside people, you'll build guardrails that make development safe and trustworthy, turning complex policy and repository management problems into clear solutions for people and artificial intelligence agents acting on their behalf.</p> <p>You'll work in one of GitLab's oldest and most complex product areas, using Vue.js and GraphQL to improve a critical system that serves GitLab.com, self-managed instances, and GitLab Dedicated. Source Code provides the interface layer, through Gitaly, to the Git repositories that account for a large portion of GitLab traffic. You'll help maintain high reliability through performance and structured query language tuning, caching, rate limiting, testing, observability, and resiliency. You'll collaborate with product management, product design, testing, security, user experience research, technical writing, Gitaly, Code Review, and Source Code Experience to deliver reliable, accessible, and performant experiences.</p> <p>Learn more about the <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/devops/create/source-code/">Create:Source Code teams</a> in the GitLab Handbook.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Develop secure, well-tested, performant features and improvements using Vue.js and GraphQL.</li> <li value="2">Turn complex requirements and legacy constraints into clear solutions without compromising the reliability of this critical system.</li> <li value="3">Partner with product management, product design, and user experience team members to understand customer problems and build intuitive, responsive, and accessible interfaces.</li> <li value="4">Collaborate across functions and teams, both asynchronously and synchronously, involving domain experts when their input will improve the outcome.</li> <li value="5">Use artificial intelligence agents for well-scoped work when they can speed up delivery without sacrificing quality, and critically review their output.</li> <li value="6">Write maintainable code that follows GitLab's standards and advocate for those standards through code review.</li> <li value="7">Strengthen reliability by monitoring production health metrics, participating in Tier 2 on-call, troubleshooting incidents, performing root cause analysis, and improving observability and resiliency.</li> <li value="8">Share knowledge through code review, technical documentation, and everyday collaboration while learning from others.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Professional experience with Vue.js or another modern JavaScript web framework, such as React, Angular, or Ember, and experience using GraphQL for application programming interface integration and data management.</li> <li value="2">A solid understanding of semantic hypertext markup language, cascading style sheets, core JavaScript concepts, responsive design, accessibility standards, and frontend performance best practices.</li> <li value="3">Experience solving complex policy, permissions, or rules-based problems in web applications and making that complexity feel simple and usable.</li> <li value="4">Experience writing frontend unit and acceptance tests with tools such as Jest, Karma, Jasmine, Mocha, ava, or tape, and familiarity with the testing pyramid.</li> <li value="5">A track record of raising the bar on how your team or group uses artificial intelligence coding agents in a large, complex monorepo, including scoping tasks, reviewing generated code, and knowing when to take direct control, paired with a clear view of where these tools fall short and how to work around it.</li> <li value="6">Experience using Git in a professional environment and familiarity with collaborative code review processes.</li> <li value="7">Clear written and spoken English communication skills, including the ability to influence without authority and share useful status updates in a remote, asynchronous environment.</li> <li value="8">The ability to manage priorities independently, work through ambiguity, take ownership, and seek guidance for decisions that are difficult to reverse.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The functional team works across Europe and North America, supporting both synchronous and asynchronous collaboration. It includes six engineers, with one frontend engineer today, so this role offers a meaningful opportunity to coach and mentor others and provide technical leadership in the frontend domain. We work closely with Code Review and Gitaly, alongside sibling teams covering Repository Sync & Interop, Source Code Experience, and Repository Scale, Performance & Git Infrastructure. We're maturing GitLab's branch protection offering while maintaining availability, reliability, and stability through bug fixes and focused technical debt work. Our roadmap includes Branch Rules, Codeowners, merge strategy options, and artificial intelligence-powered repository management and configuration.</p> <p>We welcome candidates with different levels and types of experience. title: Senior Product Manager, Agentic Source Code
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>An overview of this role</strong></span></h2> <p>GitLab is building the most comprehensive AI-powered DevSecOps platform, and this role will help shape how teams move from planning to code in an AI-native software development lifecycle.</p> <p>As Senior Product Manager, Source Code, you'll shape how planning and managing source code will evolve in an AI-native software development lifecycle. This role is focused on bringing planning and code closer together, so teams can move from requirements and specifications to commits, merge requests, and customer value with speed and quality.</p> <p>This area is evolving quickly. We're exploring how AI agents can use specifications, context, and human feedback to build the right thing, not just build the thing right. You'll define new product experiences for spec-driven, human-in-the loop development: how the link between planning intent and the code that implements it gets created, stays accurate as both change, and gets used at review time. The hard part is that this link decays. Code moves, specs might not follow, you will define how to make that connection self-maintaining.</p> <p>This is an ambiguous, high-impact opportunity for a product manager who has strong software development lifecycle knowledge, is comfortable working with technical teams, and wants to help create something new in DevSecOps.</p> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>What You’ll Do</strong></span></h2> <ul> <li>Define and drive product strategy for experiences that connect planning, source code management, and AI-assisted development.</li> <li>Shape workflows where teams and agents move between intent and code in both directions, so a specification can be traced to the merges that implement it and a diff can be read and reviewed against the intent behind it.</li> <li>Work with engineering, design, and other product teams to build product experiences that support human-in-the-loop and autonomous development workflows.</li> <li>Partner with teams working on demos and prototypes, including near-term work around spec-driven planning and autonomous development modes, including which decisions stay with a human and why.</li> <li>Use customer insights, product usage data, and market context to identify opportunities that can deliver customer value quickly.</li> <li>Help teams ship fast with quality, balancing near-term execution with longer-term product direction.</li> <li>Explore how planning can better account for reviewing code, reviewing test cases, and validating that work produced by agents matches the intended outcome.</li> <li>Collaborate across Plan, Source Code Management, Code Review, and AI product areas to reduce friction across the software development lifecycle.</li> </ul> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>What You’ll Bring</strong></span></h2> <ul> <li>Experience as a product manager working on developer tools, DevOps tools, source code management, planning tools, AI-native products, or related software development lifecycle products.</li> <li>Direct, hands-on experience with the source code lifecycle, including branches, merge requests, code review, CI/CD, and releases, whether as a product manager or as an engineer, along with a strong understanding of how software moves from ideas and requirements through planning, coding, review, testing, and delivery.</li> <li>Experience working with technical product areas and engineering teams, with enough technical depth to understand developer workflows and tradeoffs.</li> <li>A data-forward approach to product management, including experience using data to identify customer impact and guide prioritization.</li> <li>Comfort operating in ambiguous spaces where there may not yet be a clear market pattern or established product category.</li> <li>Experience building or shipping with AI tools and agents, not just using them, and a point of view of your own on where AI helps and where it does not across the software development lifecycle.</li> <li>Ability to think creatively about how AI changes the software development lifecycle and how product experiences should adapt.</li> <li>Strong collaboration and communication skills, especially in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.</li> <li>A bias toward action and the ability to help teams ship meaningful customer value quickly.</li> </ul> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>About the team</strong></span></h2> <p>This role sits within the Product organization and will work closely with teams across Plan, Source Code Management, Code Review, and AI. We are focused on helping GitLab customers plan, build, and deliver software in a faster, more connected way.</p> <p>You'll join a group that is rethinking how planning and coding should work as AI changes the speed and shape of software development. Rather than treating planning, coding, and review as separate stages, we're exploring how to bring these workflows closer together so humans and agents can collaborate more effectively.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. title: Senior Product Manager, CRM & GTM Systems
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p><strong>An Overview about the Role</strong></p> <p>We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the Lead-to-Opportunity (L2O) domain within our Salesforce and GTM technology ecosystem. This role sits at the intersection of marketing operations, sales process, and technology owning the roadmap for how leads are captured, scored, routed, and converted into pipeline, and how our broader GTM tech stack supports that motion.</p> <p>This is a foundational hire one of the first product managers on a team actively transforming from a reactive BSA model into a proactive, roadmap-driven product organization. You'll be both an individual contributor driving your own domain and a mentor helping BSAs grow into product manager roles. You'll have direct influence over how we shape the team's future operating model.</p> <p><strong>What You'll Do</strong></p> <p><strong>Internal Product Roadmap Ownership</strong></p> <ul> <li>Define, own, and maintain the multi-quarter internal product roadmap for the Lead-to-Opportunity domain covering lead capture, enrichment, scoring, routing, conversion, opportunity and the broader GTM technology stack integrated with Salesforce</li> <li>Translate business strategy from Marketing, Sales Development, RevOps, and GTM leadership into sequenced, prioritized system capabilities with clear outcomes and success metrics</li> <li>Define the domain's strategic priorities each quarter and half, balancing net-new capability delivery, stabilization, and technical debt reduction with transparent trade-off frameworks</li> <li>Drive quarterly planning ceremonies, partnering with Engineering Managers and BSAs to align capacity with roadmap commitments</li> <li>Own domain-level documentation: process maps, current-vs-future state lead lifecycle flows, and decision logs that keep stakeholders and the team aligned on scope and ownership</li> </ul> <p><strong>Stakeholder Partnership & Requirements Translation</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the primary product voice for all L2O and GTM Systems initiatives, partnering closely with Marketing, Marketing Operations, SDR/BDR leadership, Sales, and RevOps</li> <li>Lead discovery, requirements workshops, and business process design sessions translating complex GTM and marketing operations requirements into actionable system specifications</li> <li>Own the decision layer between "what the business needs" and "what engineering builds," resolving ambiguity with structured frameworks and documented decisions</li> <li>Run structured stakeholder alignment sessions to surface trade-offs, build consensus, and drive open decisions to closure rather than letting them linger</li> <li>Represent the domain in cross-team planning and leadership reviews able to explain technical constraints to business stakeholders and business context to engineers</li> </ul> <p><strong>Team Mentorship & Capability Building</strong></p> <ul> <li>Act as a product craft mentor and senior thought partner for the BSA team, actively upskilling analysts in product thinking, requirements structuring, acceptance criteria definition, and roadmap communication</li> <li>Model and codify what "good" looks like reusable templates, rituals (backlog grooming, roadmap reviews), and a rubric BSAs can grow against</li> <li>Give BSAs increasing ownership over pieces of the roadmap as they develop, with regular feedback and structured check-ins</li> <li>Partner with leadership to evolve the team's operating model from project-execution-focused to product-thinking-led, raising the bar for how EntApps delivers business value</li> </ul> <p><strong>Program Strategy & Delivery Oversight</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead initiatives end-to-end: discovery, requirements, prioritization, solution design review, UAT, launch, and post-launch measurement</li> <li>Write and maintain clear user stories, acceptance criteria, and lead-flow and data-flow diagrams that engineering and admins can build against without ambiguity</li> <li>Manage a healthy, well-groomed backlog intake requests from Marketing and Sales Development, triage by impact and effort, and defend prioritization decisions to stakeholders</li> <li>Define success metrics per initiative (lead response time, routing accuracy, lead-to-opportunity conversion rate, data quality, SDR/BDR adoption) and report on outcomes, not just delivery</li> <li>Identify and de-risk dependencies across adjacent domains campaign operations, data enrichment vendors, opportunity handoff to sales before they block delivery</li> <li>Own UAT strategy and acceptance criteria in collaboration with BSAs, ensuring system changes meet business requirements before production release</li> </ul> <p><strong>Systems Architecture Collaboration</strong></p> <ul> <li>Partner with Enterprise Architects and Engineering Managers on Salesforce and MarTech integration design marketing automation platform to Salesforce sync, data enrichment pipelines, lead scoring and routing engines, ensuring choices hold up to governance, scale, and future roadmap needs</li> <li>Bring informed opinions on GTM platform architecture trade-offs based on deep domain knowledge</li> <li>Stay current on platform roadmaps for Salesforce Sales Cloud and connected MarTech tools, identifying opportunities to leverage native capabilities before custom builds</li> <li>Maintain domain-level R&R clarity, who owns what across US/India technical managers, BSAs, and adjacent pods and update as team and scope evolve</li> <li>Ability to engage deeply with engineering and architecture teams on API design, data modeling, and integration patterns.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You'll Bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>7+ years in Salesforce product management, business systems analysis, or Marketing/Revenue Operations technology roles, with demonstrated growth into product ownership</li> <li>Strong working knowledge of Lead-to-Opportunity processes; lead capture, scoring, routing, and conversion and how they connect marketing execution to sales pipeline</li> <li>Hands-on familiarity with the GTM technology stack: Salesforce Sales Cloud plus marketing automation platforms (Marketo, HubSpot, or Pardot), lead scoring and routing tools, and data enrichment or intent providers</li> <li>Good Understanding of quoting process </li> <li>Demonstrated ability to own and communicate multi-quarter internal product roadmaps to senior business and technology stakeholders</li> <li>Proven experience leading initiatives end-to-end with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities, especially across Marketing and Sales</li> <li>Sufficient technical fluency to engage meaningfully with engineering on API design, data model decisions, and integration trade-offs — without needing to write code</li> <li>Experience mentoring or upskilling analysts and BSAs, you enjoy developing people, not just managing tickets</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication; able to represent technical trade-offs to non-technical executives and translate business asks into clear technical requirements</li> <li>Comfortable operating in ambiguity and driving structure where none exists</li> <li>Experience with AI-assisted development workflows, data governance and compliance for lead data, or prior people-management experience</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the Team</strong></p> <p>You'll be one of the first product managers on a team actively transforming from a reactive BSA function into a proactive, roadmap-driven product organization. The Lead-to-Opportunity domain sits at the top of GitLab's revenue funnel; the quality of data, routing, and conversion here affects every downstream system and every seller. Getting this right is not an IT problem; it's a revenue problem. You'll have direct influence over how we shape the team's future operating model and how the next generation of BSAs grows into product managers.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our <a class="waffle-rich-text-link" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/" data-sheets-formula-bar-text-link="https://bit.ly/GLBeneUS" data-sheets-formula-bar-text-style="font-size:12px;color:#1155cc;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:underline;font-family:''Arial'';font-style:normal;text-decoration-skip-ink:none;">benefits</a><span data-sheets-formula-bar-text-style="font-size:12px;color:#000000;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;font-family:'Arial';font-style:normal;text-decoration-skip-ink:none;"> and </span><a class="waffle-rich-text-link" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/stock-options/" data-sheets-formula-bar-text-link="https://bit.ly/GLequity" data-sheets-formula-bar-text-style="font-size:12px;color:#1155cc;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:underline;font-family:''Arial'';font-style:normal;text-decoration-skip-ink:none;">equity</a>. Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary.</em></p></div><div class="title">Uni

customer engagements at once, either as the primary engineer or as a lead providing oversight and direction to other engineers.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> with two or more cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), or Microsoft Azure.</li> <li>Experience using, deploying, or configuring GitLab, including a solid understanding of Git and source control workflows.</li> <li>Strong grounding in Security / AI technologies</li> <li>Experience delivering customer-facing services such as installation, migration, training, and advisory engagements across GitLab's feature set.</li> <li>Proven ability to independently manage one or more projects and to lead and provide direction to other Professional Services Engineers on complex engagements.</li> <li>Strong communication skills in English, written and verbal, with the ability to provide clear status updates and build consensus with peers and customers in Requests may include user migrations, de-duplication, Renewal Manager ownership changes, compensation exceptions, and Salesforce or data issues.</li> <li>Raise the operating standard in your domain by documenting processes, mentoring others on how the renewal motion works, and contributing to broader Revenue Operations initiatives that need the renewals perspective.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience in Renewals Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, management consulting, strategy, or a similar analytical and problem-solving role, with ownership of operational improvements and cross-functional initiatives.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with both consumption and subscription renewal motions, including renewal forecasting, retention reporting, and the contractual and process mechanics that govern how renewals close.</li> <li>Strong critical thinking and structured problem-solving skills. Measure their impact on pipeline hygiene, data quality, forecast accuracy, and bookings, and change the cadence where it isn't working.</li> <li>Work with other Revenue Strategy & Operations teams, Finance, Product, Data, and Enablement to deliver changes from the first draft through field adoption. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <p>GitLab's Security Risk function is responsible for reducing risk across the security division: third-party risk (TPRM), annual security risk assessments, quarterly risk reporting, and remediation of security findings. Reporting to the Security Risk Manager, you will bring expertise on risk methodology, risk-based thinking, and AI-enablement. </p> <p>In this role, you'll partner closely with Security, Legal, IT, Product, and Engineering to translate technical findings and vendor risk into business-relevant risk statements and risk treatments. You’ll help surface emerging risks, and report top risks to leadership. </p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li>Building and maintaining a risk register that translates technical vulnerabilities, control gaps, and third-party risk findings into quantified, business-relevant risk statements.</li> <li>Driving cross-functional remediation of security findings and risk issues to closure, tracked against SLAs.</li> <li>Driving automation and AI-enabled improvements for risk and GRC workflows so the team can spend less time on manual work and more time on high-value risk analysis and program maturity.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you'll do</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Own risk identification, analysis, and prioritization across third-party risk (TPRM), security risk assessments, and security findings, using an established risk framework (e.g., NIST RMF, ISO 31000, or NIST 800-39). </li> <li>Translate technical vulnerabilities, control gaps, and risk findings into clear, quantified risk statements that non-security stakeholders and leadership can act on. </li> <li>Drive remediation of findings and risk exceptions to closure, partnering with Engineering, IT, Product, and Legal, and escalating stalled or high-severity items. </li> <li>Mature and maintain a risk register and quarterly reporting cadence that gives leadership clear visibility into open risk, remediation progress, and trends.</li> <li>Own and mature AI risk management, including AI impact assessments, AI risk assessments, and risk treatments, to support ISO 42001 certification.</li> <li>Design, develop, and implement key risk indicators and supporting metrics for top risks in the risk register.</li> <li>Identify manual, repetitive steps in risk and TPRM workflows and personally build the automation, scripting, or AI-enabled tooling to remove them. </li> <li>Contribute to the roadmap for the risk program, incorporating new frameworks, regulatory changes, and lessons learned from past assessments.</li> <li>Monitor the internal and external risk landscape (new frameworks, threat trends, business changes) to identify and escalate emerging risks before they become findings.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience in security risk management, working with security-centric risk management or compliance frameworks (e.g., NIST RMF, NIST 800-39, ISO 31000). Familiarity with AI governance frameworks (e.g., ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF) is a plus.</li> <li>Experience designing and executing qualitative and quantitative risk analyses that translate technical risks into measurable business impact. </li> <li>A track record of driving risk assessments, risk registers, and remediation efforts to closure across IT, Procurement, Internal Audit, Legal, Product, and Engineering, in a heavily regulated or multi-entity environment.</li> <li>Experience interpreting technical control requirements and translating them for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.</li> <li>Demonstrated bias toward automation: you've personally built scripts, workflows, or AI-enabled tooling that reduced manual risk or GRC work, not just evaluated tools conceptually. </li> <li>Comfort operating with ambiguity, managing multiple concurrent assessments, and reprioritizing under tight deadlines. </li> <li>Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with demonstrated ability to translate security risks into business risks.</li> <li>Strong understanding of cloud security, SaaS security models, and DevSecOps practices.</li> <li>Relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC) are preferred but not required. </li> </ul> <h4><strong>About the team</strong></h4> <p>The <strong>Security Assurance </strong>organization helps GitLab build and maintain trust by strengthening how we approach security, compliance, and risk across the company. The Security Risk team sits within that group and owns third-party risk (TPRM), security risk assessments, and remediation of security findings. The Security Risk Team performs thorough, collaborative, and efficient risk assessments as well as drive risk reduction so that GitLab can achieve its goals while maintaining a high level of security. Security Risk counterparts are Security Compliance, Security Governance and Security Enablement functions.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. On the dependency analysis side, you teach the analysis engine what a project depends on. You parse dependency manifests, lockfiles, and SBOMs so the engine knows which libraries and frameworks are in play and how the code uses them. You also extend the service that turns security advisories into automated merge requests that update vulnerable dependencies. On the vulnerability detection side, you grow GitLab's security analysis engine with hybrid analyzers that blend rule-based detection and AI reasoning. You build and apply the tooling that develops, evaluates, and ships those analyzers, and you measure how well they find real problems. That work also expands coverage of the libraries, frameworks, and AI agent tooling that real-world applications are built on.</p> <p>These threads reinforce each other. What a project depends on, and how its code uses those dependencies, are parts of one picture, and this team works across all of it. We make thoughtful use of AI-assisted development tools in our daily work. We expect you to use them effectively and with good judgment.</p> <h3><strong>What you do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for team initiatives from design through delivery, shipping with minimal guidance in partnership with the technical lead</li> <li>Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review</li> <li>Design and ship analyzers that pair deterministic analysis capabilities with AI-driven analysis, and build the evaluation harnesses that measure their false positives and missed findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. You'll join the Engineering department and work directly with customers as they encounter edge cases. You'll dig into Linux systems, logs, and our Ruby on Rails codebase to troubleshoot performance issues, reproduce bugs, and contribute merge requests that fix problems at the source.</p> <p>You'll also improve our documentation, refine support processes in our issue tracker, and collaborate closely with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales so customer feedback directly shapes our roadmap. In your first year, you'll build deep expertise across a range of GitLab implementations, strengthen our ability to keep customers productive on both self-managed GitLab and GitLab.com software as a service, and help create tools and content that make support more efficient and effective for the entire team.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/gitlab-detective">A tool to automatically check a GitLab Omnibus install for known issues</a></li> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/gitlabsos">A solution to capture the state of a customer’s server for easier troubleshooting</a></li> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/sosparser">A tool which turns log files into interactive tables to easily sort and filter columns</a></li> <li><a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/chatops/">A ChatOps feature that makes it easier to identify user accounts on GitLab.com</a></li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Act as an escalation point for difficult customer interactions and lead the resolution of complex issues through Zendesk tickets, merge requests, email, and video calls.</li> <li>Mentor and guide teammates on complex troubleshooting and customer communication through pairing sessions and cross-team collaboration.</li> <li>Advocate for and drive improvements to support practices, product quality, and reusable documentation and support content that directly influence team objectives.</li> <li>Collaborate with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales teams to shape product goals, roadmaps, and priorities while driving fixes and new features.</li> <li>Participate in regular weekday and weekend on-call rotations during daytime hours, providing emergency support for self-managed GitLab and software as a service customers and coordinating incident communications with the GitLab.com Production team.</li> <li>Participate in hiring by reviewing applications and assessments and joining interviews to help grow the Support team.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience owning complex, customer-facing technical cases from initial contact through triage, reproduction, bug reporting, resolution, and clear customer communication, including difficult or escalated interactions.</li> <li>Strong experience with Linux systems administration, scripting, Git, and continuous integration and continuous delivery in production or customer environments, with the ability to investigate issues at both the infrastructure and application levels.</li> <li>Ability to mentor teammates on complex troubleshooting and customer communication through pairing sessions, case reviews, and cross-team collaboration.</li> <li>Experience collaborating with Product, Engineering, and Sales teams to turn customer feedback into product fixes, feature improvements, and roadmap priorities.</li> <li>Familiarity with DevOps practices and technologies such as Kubernetes and serverless computing, and an understanding of how different GitLab implementations operate and affect customers.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to learn, collaborate across teams, and apply transferable skills from related technical support or engineering roles.</li> <li>Fluent Korean language skills (required)</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> title: Site Reliability Engineer, Infrastructure Platforms — AMER (Intermediate to Senior Staff)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p><strong>An overview of this role</strong></p> <p>Site Reliability Engineers keep GitLab's user-facing services and production systems running reliably at scale. They combine software engineering with operational excellence, applying sound engineering principles, automation, and continuous improvement to build, operate, and evolve our production infrastructure.</p> <p>This is a single application for Site Reliability Engineering opportunities across Infrastructure Platforms. Rather than asking you to choose the right team or level upfront, we evaluate your skills holistically and match you to the opportunity that best aligns with your experience and our hiring needs. We hire Site Reliability Engineers from Intermediate through Senior Staff across multiple Infrastructure Platforms teams.</p> <p>We don't expect every candidate to have experience with every technology in our environment. We're looking for engineers with strong technical fundamentals, a growth mindset, and the ability to learn quickly. We'll support you in becoming successful with GitLab's tools, systems, and ways of working.</p> <p><strong><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Please note: This position is open to candidates based in the United States and Canada only. Candidates based in the United Kingdom can apply to this posting:</span> <a href="https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/gitlab/jobs/8773546002">Site Reliability Engineer, Infrastructure Platforms — UK (Intermediate to Senior Staff)</a></strong></p> <p><strong>How our SRE hiring works</strong></p> <p>Because this is a single application for SRE roles across Infrastructure Platforms, our process is built to evaluate you once and match you well, rather than interviewing separately for every team.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Recruiter Screen:</strong> A conversation about your background, what you're looking for, and the level and teams that fit, so we can point your process in the right direction.</li> <li><strong>Core Technical: </strong>The shared assessment every SRE candidate takes, regardless of eventual team. A low-stress, collaborative discussion covering system architecture and incident review.</li> <li><strong>Hiring Manager Interview: </strong>A conversation about ownership, judgment, execution, collaboration, and growth, the non-technical signals that make an SRE effective at GitLab.</li> <li><strong>Peer Technical: </strong>Team-specific depth, run by SREs from the team you're most likely to join, focused on the problems that team actually works on.</li> <li><strong>Skip-Level Interview: </strong>A conversation with a senior leader on values alignment, and how you'll work across teams.</li> </ul> <p>After your interviews, we consider your performance alongside our current hiring needs to confirm the level and team where you'll do your best work. Interview results are a major factor, and final placement also reflects our active hiring priorities at the time.</p> <p><strong>We’ll calibrate your level throughout the interview process based on the scope and impact of your experience.</strong></p> <ul> <li>Intermediate: You independently deliver meaningful reliability improvements within a defined area.</li> <li>Senior: You own complex reliability work end to end and raise the effectiveness of your team.</li> <li>Staff: You shape reliability across multiple teams, solving systemic problems and creating approaches others can reuse.</li> <li>Senior Staff: You set technical direction across a broader Infrastructure area and influence reliability strategy at organizational scale.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What you'll do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Keep user-facing services and production systems reliable, scalable, and efficient</li> <li>Build automation and tooling that reduces toil and replaces manual work with repeatable, infrastructure-as-code-driven workflows</li> <li>Operate and troubleshoot production systems on Kubernetes, including deployments, rollouts, and scaling</li> <li>Write and maintain infrastructure as code, and ship changes safely through CI/CD and GitOps</li> <li>Participate in on-call, triage alerts, follow and improve runbooks, and escalate appropriately</li> <li>Contribute to the observability stack, using metrics, logs, and SLOs to detect symptoms early rather than just outages</li> <li>Take part in incident response and post-incident reviews, turning learnings into changes in automation and process</li> <li>Document runbooks, architecture decisions, and reviews so your findings become repeatable practices</li> </ul> <p><strong>What you'll bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience keeping production systems reliable, combining an operations mindset with real software engineering practice</li> <li>Experience building net-new infrastructure tooling and automation, not just configuring existing tools. For example, Terraform modules, Kubernetes operators or controllers, or production automation and services written from scratch</li> <li>The ability to read, debug, and reason about code. Most of our teams work in Go; some work in Ruby. You can discuss a piece of code's behavior, performance, and failure modes</li> <li>Experience with infrastructure as code, and with Kubernetes and its ecosystem, at a depth appropriate to your level</li> <li>Hands-on experience with at least one major cloud provider (GCP or AWS)</li> <li>Familiarity with observability practices, including metrics, logging, alerting, and SLOs or SLIs, and using data to inform operational decisions</li> <li>Comfort participating in on-call and incident response, with a structured approach to troubleshooting under pressure</li> <li>Strong written communication and the ability to operate as a manager-of-one in an async, distributed environment</li> <li>A track record of using automation, and increasingly AI, to reduce toil and improve how you and your team work</li> <li>Alignment with GitLab's values and a commitment to working in accordance with them</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/infrastructure-platforms/">Infrastructure Platforms</a> is responsible for the availability, reliability, performance, and scalability of GitLab’s user-facing services, most notably <a href="http://GitLab.com" target="_blank">GitLab.com</a>. The organization spans teams across <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/infrastructure-platforms/production-engineering/">Production Engineering</a>, <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/infrastructure-platforms/gitlab-dedicated/">GitLab Dedicated</a>, <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/infrastructure-platforms/gitlab-delivery/">GitLab Delivery</a>, and <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/infrastructure-platforms/developer-experience/">Developer Experience</a>, covering everything from the production fleet and networking platform to observability, incident response, deployment infrastructure, tenant scale, and our single-tenant Dedicated offering.<br><br>We are a globally distributed, remote-first organization that works asynchronously, favors automation over toil, and uses monitoring, metrics, and clear ownership to continuously improve the reliability of GitLab at scale. For more on how we work, see the <a href="https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/gitlab/jobs/INSERT_URL_HERE">Infrastructure Handbook Page</a>.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. <li>Build and manage relationships with nonprofit organizations, universities, and program members.</li> <li>Oversee day-to-day operations for both programs, streamline processes, and improve appropriate support resources.</li> <li>Partner with Sales and Marketing to grow program membership and improve renewal rates.</li> <li>Create resources that help GitLab team members and the wider trends, conduct benchmarking, and establish best practices for social impact and community initiatives.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience managing corporate social responsibility, social impact, community advocacy, or related programs.</li> <li>Experience managing in-kind donation programs.</li> <li>An analytical, data-driven approach to building community programs.</li> <li>Written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex concepts into clear, engaging messages.</li> <li>Organizational skills, creative problem-solving, and resourcefulness, with the ability to prioritize work, meet deadlines, and maintain attention to detail.</li> <li>Experience initiating and leading projects across internal and title: Staff Backend Engineer, Architecture Engineering: Nonlinear Productivity
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Staff Engineer, you'll be the technical anchor for GitLab's Nonlinear Productivity team in the US: the person who decides what "proven" means before something ships, and who helps shape what the team builds next, not just how to build it. It's a from-scratch, generalist team with no dedicated product manager — that ownership starts on day one.</p> <p>Some examples of the problems this team takes on:</p> <ul> <li>Cutting the time it takes to complete a good code review — one that still keeps a human in the loop — by half, using agentic solutions.</li> <li>Turning a manual, error-prone release step into an agentic workflow that catches its own mistakes before a human ever has to.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Set the technical direction for the team's agentic systems, from how agents are orchestrated to where a step should stay human-owned, and defend those calls once they're tested against real code.</li> <li>Discover and prioritize sources of friction across GitLab's SDLC, driving the fix — agentic, process-based, or both — from a rough hypothesis through to a shipped, measured result.</li> <li>Work across any part of GitLab's codebase as the problem requires, since this team operates like a small, generalist group rather than one scoped to a single service.</li> <li>Apply distributed systems judgment to catch cases where generated code looks correct but breaks under concurrency, at scale, or across deployment topologies (including self-managed, dedicated, and multi-tenant environments), and coach others to do the same.</li> <li>Mentor senior and mid-level engineers on agent engineering practices and distributed systems judgment, through design reviews and pairing that raise the team's collective bar rather than just your own output.</li> <li>Collaborate with the India-based group a few times a week to align on the roadmap, and represent the team's technical progress to stakeholders in the Chief Technology Officer's organization.</li> <li>Serve as a bar raiser for the team's hiring, owning the Technical Leadership round for other Staff-level candidates as the team scales.</li> <li>Own a greenfield technical foundation from day one, with your scope and impact free to grow as the team scales.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience building reliable agentic or large language model (LLM)-based systems, including multi-step orchestration, tool use, guardrails, and recovery.</li> <li>Ability to work autonomously in unfamiliar codebases and drive solutions from discovery through completion.</li> <li>Strong distributed systems and computer science fundamentals, including coordination, consistency, idempotency, rate limiting, failure modes, and degradation under load.</li> <li>Proficiency in Go, Rust, or Python, with the ability to read and modify code in the others.</li> <li>A track record of delivering results from unclear or incomplete requirements — able to take a complex, loosely specified problem and decompose it into a concrete proposal of small, shippable steps.</li> <li>Experience designing evaluation frameworks for systems where "looks plausible" and "is actually correct" are different questions, and a track record of raising the quality bar for a team's output, not just your own.</li> <li>A history of unblocking and enabling teammates — through design reviews, technical writing, or mentoring — and of engaging regularly with other teams to find where collaboration actually pays off.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Nonlinear Productivity — shortened internally to "NLP," with no relation to natural language processing — is one of GitLab's newest teams: a strategic incubation group that reports into AI Platform leadership under the direct sponsorship of the CTO. It's split into a US group (this role) and an India-based group working the same charter; the two sync on roadmap and tooling a few times a week but otherwise run day to day on their own. Solutions that prove out internally are the team's path to a monetized, customer-facing GitLab offering.</p> <p>It's a good fit for engineers who want technical ownership of something with no existing playbook, and a hand in defining a brand-new part of GitLab from its first commit.</p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. <ul> <li value="1">A record of leading technical work across more than one team or a broad product area.</li> <li value="2">Deep backend architecture and production experience with complex event-driven boundaries.</li> <li value="4">Experience building alignment through clear written proposals and decision records so teams document, understand, and adopt technical decisions.</li> <li value="5">Experience making trade-offs among customer outcomes, delivery speed, technical health, reliability, and long-term platform investment.</li> <li value="6">Experience mentoring engineers and description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As a Senior or Staff Backend Engineer with the <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/">Database Excellence group</a>, you'll build and evolve database automation and PostgreSQL as a service capabilities for GitLab. The level will be determined during the hiring process. You'll use Go to automate the full lifecycle of PostgreSQL across GitLab's infrastructure, making database operations safer, more consistent, and easier to scale for databases that sit behind high-throughput, always-on internet services. You'll work closely with partner teams to shape how GitLab provisions and manages PostgreSQL in a fully remote, highly collaborative environment.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li value="1"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/database-team/traffic-replay-poc">SQL Traffic Replay Tooling</a>, which validates upgrades and changes against real production workloads.</li> <li value="2"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/database-team/backend/-/work_items/1">PostgreSQL as a Service Platform</a>, which provides standardized, automated provisioning and lifecycle management for internal product databases.</li> <li value="3"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-com/gl-infra/data-access/dbo/-/work_items/75">PostgreSQL Major Version Upgrade Automation</a>, which supports safe, repeatable major upgrades at GitLab.com scale.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Design, build, and maintain Go-based automation that manages the full PostgreSQL lifecycle, including provisioning, configuration, upgrades, failover, scaling, and decommissioning, reducing reactive operational work that currently takes more than 80% of the team's time.</li> <li value="2">Build automation that works across infrastructure-as-code tooling and cloud infrastructure, and evaluate operator-based approaches as the platform evolves.</li> <li value="3">Use AI agents as a regular part of building and operating services, including implementation, review, and reducing repetitive work, while keeping the context agents need in the repository so the whole team can build on it.</li> <li value="4">Build for internet scale by designing automation and services for high-throughput, always-on production workloads, where GitLab.com traffic sets the bar for correctness, latency, and availability.</li> <li value="5">Integrate compute, storage, networking, identity and access management, and managed data services across cloud providers into one coherent PostgreSQL platform instead of creating bespoke setups for each database.</li> <li value="6">Build GitLab's PostgreSQL as a service platform to replace bespoke database setups with standardized, automated provisioning and lifecycle management, so supporting more databases doesn't require growing the operations team at the same rate.</li> <li value="7">Collaborate closely with product management, infrastructure, software delivery, and other engineering teams to design and ship high-performing solutions.</li> <li value="8">Research, design, and implement improvements to PostgreSQL performance, scalability, and data health, helping maintain more than 8 months of operational runway for all critical database saturation points.</li> <li value="9">Review database automation and Go changes from other engineers and contributors, with attention to safety, maintainability, and performance.</li> <li value="10">Document automation practices, PostgreSQL operational patterns, and guidance that helps engineers use and contribute to the platform.</li> <li value="11">Build safe, repeatable automation for PostgreSQL major version upgrades at GitLab.com scale, validating changes against real production traffic before rollout.</li> <li of stateful services, especially databases. This role will work across the entire group to help us identify and remove the biggest points of friction that affect development at GitLab. Expect to split your time between hands-on coding in Ruby and Go, designing scalable solutions and helping every team deliver.  You’ll be instrumental in shaping our engineering culture across GitLab.  </p> <p>This is a highly visible role with strong company-wide support. projects</strong></h3> <ul> <li> <div><strong>Project Examples</strong><br>In this role, you may lead projects such as:</div> <ul> <li><strong>Internal developer platform adoption:</strong> Build and environments:</strong> Build development, CI, and test environments that reflect production Kubernetes behavior — including third-party operators and the custom resources services depend on — sequencing CRD establishment, controller readiness, and dependent workloads so engineers get a working environment rather than a partially reconciled one, across both local and remote clusters.</li> <li><strong>Platform reliability and observability:</strong> Partner with infrastructure and service teams to improve rollout safety, troubleshooting, service health, resource management, and operational visibility across Kubernetes workloads.</li> </ul> <div><strong>What You'll Do</strong></div> <ul> <li>Lead and grow a team responsible for developer tooling and internal platform capabilities used by engineering teams to build and operate services.</li> <li>Set and execute a roadmap for Kubernetes-based developer workflows, balancing developer experience, platform reliability, security, and operational efficiency.</li> <li>Guide the design of reusable onboarding and deployment patterns for services running on Kubernetes, including workloads, networking, configuration and secrets, identity, storage, observability, progressive delivery, and the custom resources and controllers that services depend on.</li> <li>Make environment bring-up and teardown deterministic — resolving readiness and ordering dependencies between CRDs, controllers, and the workloads that rely on them — so engineers get reproducible environments instead of intermittent failures.</li> <li>Partner with infrastructure, security, and application teams to turn Kubernetes capabilities into simple, well-supported workflows rather than requiring every service team to become a Kubernetes expert.</li> <li>Establish engineering standards, documentation, automation, and feedback loops that improve adoption and reduce the time required to bring a service from development to production.</li> <li>Coach engineers through architectural decisions, incident follow-up, and production operations while maintaining a clear focus on sustainable team delivery.</li> <li>Represent the team with technical and organizational stakeholders, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and use adoption and reliability measures to guide prioritization.</li> </ul> <div><strong>What You'll Bring</strong></div> <ul> <li>Deep experience building developer tooling, DevEx platforms, testing frameworks, or CI/CD systems at scale.</li> <li>Strong hands-on Go experience designing, implementing, testing, and operating production-quality services, command-line tools, automation, or platform tooling. Experience contributing to Ruby-based systems is also valuable for this role.</li> <li>Practical Kubernetes experience building or operating production workloads and platform capabilities, including deployments, services, networking, configuration and secrets, observability, resource management, and troubleshooting.</li> <li><strong>Depth in Kubernetes deployment lifecycle: Helm-based deployment and release management, kubeconfig and multi-cluster context handling including deploying into clusters you don't own, and integrating third-party operators and their custom resources (CloudNativePG, cert-manager and similar) into working environments — including the readiness and ordering problems that come with them: waiting on CRD establishment, controller availability, and custom resources reaching their own definition of ready. Experience authoring a controller or operator is useful but not required.</strong></li> <li>Experience designing scalable solutions that improve engineering productivity, test reliability, development environments, or delivery workflows across multiple teams.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to provide technical leadership and influence without authority across engineering, infrastructure, security, and product functions.</li> <li>Familiarity with DevOps workflows, CI/CD pipelines, release automation, and production operations.</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication skills in a remote-first environment.</li> <li>A product mindset with a passion for empowering developers through simple, reliable, and well-documented workflows.</li> <li>Alignment with GitLab values, especially collaboration, iteration, and transparency.</li> </ul> </li> </ul><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. As a Staff-level pricing and commercialization expert, you'll design, scale, and drive GitLab's enterprise monetization and commercial buying programs as an individual contributor at the top of our individual contributor track. You'll serve as the architect of our Enterprise Agreements, cloud marketplace and channel pricing structures, and competitive commercial programs, partnering across Product, go-to-market (GTM), Finance, Sales, Renewals, Product Marketing, Partners, and Deal Desk to turn pricing decisions into scalable programs that work for customers and the field.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll competitors in the DevSecOps and AI tooling market.</li> <li>Own list-to-net price realization strategy across products, geographic regions, GTM segments, and routes to market.</li> <li>Partner with Product Management, Product Marketing, and GTM leaders to shape new packaging and pricing proposals, evaluate monetization models as GitLab's AI and platform capabilities evolve, and bring data-backed recommendations to cross-functional and executive stakeholders.</li> <li>Act as the go-to expert for pricing enablement by building training, playbooks, and battlecards that give the field confidence in pricing conversations and help them explain commercial value.</li> <li>Put commercial programs into practice in partnership with Deal Desk, Revenue Operations, and Data teams, staying hands-on with execution as well as strategy.</li> <li>Define, launch, and scale Enterprise Agreements and marketed bundling strategies that simplify transactions, encourage multi-product and GitLab Duo adoption, and maximize customer lifetime value.</li> <li>Define channel and marketplace pricing strategy, including tiering, discounting frameworks, and margin structures, across resellers, global systems integrators, independent software vendors, and cloud marketplaces such as Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud Platform, and Microsoft Azure.</li> <li>Document decisions and frameworks in the GitLab handbook and default to asynchronous, written communication as part of GitLab's all-remote, globally distributed team.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Extensive experience across strategy consulting, pricing, strategic finance, or corporate or deal strategy, ideally at a software as a service or enterprise software company.</li> <li>Deep experience in monetization or pricing strategy, including direct ownership of pricing waterfalls, enterprise buying programs such as Enterprise License Agreements or Enterprise Agreements, or channel and marketplace pricing models.</li> <li>A track record of operating as a go-to expert without formal authority. Other teams bring you difficult pricing questions, and your recommendations carry weight with senior stakeholders because of the thinking and evidence behind them.</li> <li>Hands-on work with AI agents and automations that real teams used in production</li> <li>A bias toward iteration and shipping. You're comfortable making a strategic call, documenting the reasoning, and adjusting as new data comes in instead of waiting for perfect information.</li> <li>Strong written communication skills and the ability to work independently in an asynchronous, all-remote environment while driving cross-functional agreement.</li> <li>Experience partnering with and influencing senior stakeholders across Product, Sales, and Finance, including vice president and senior vice president levels, as an individual contributor.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Pricing Strategy team shapes how GitLab packages, prices, and commercializes its product portfolio. This role sits within Corporate Security Engineering and focuses on building secure-by-default controls for endpoints and the SaaS platforms that support them, with a strong emphasis on macOS. You'll own meaningful technical decisions around endpoint hardening, automation, and detection, and you'll help turn security requirements into scalable engineering systems that are measurable, auditable, and designed to reduce friction for end users.</p> <p>This is a strong fit if you're motivated by solving security problems with code. You will work across endpoint management, identity, and security operations to improve how GitLab manages macOS, iOS, Windows, and Linux devices through Infrastructure-as-Code, Terraform, and GitOps workflows. In your first year, you'll be expected to strengthen endpoint security architecture, expand automation, and improve the reliability and auditability of how controls are deployed and maintained.</p> <h4><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Lead the security architecture of GitLab's endpoint fleet and related infrastructure, with a primary focus on macOS.</li> <li>Design and support automation for secure endpoint deployment, configuration, and lifecycle management using code-based workflows.</li> <li>Manage endpoint and SaaS security configuration through Terraform, version control, merge requests, continuous integration pipelines, and automated rollouts.</li> <li>Define and enforce security baselines across macOS, iOS, Windows, and Linux endpoints.</li> <li>Develop patching and software distribution approaches that align with security, compliance, and operational requirements.</li> <li>Partner with Information Technology, Security Operations, and Detection and Response teams to improve endpoint telemetry, detections, and response models.</li> <li>Drive process improvements that reduce manual work and lower risk by favoring automation, policy-driven controls, and auditable change management.</li> <li>Mentor engineers across Corporate Security and Information Technology, and serve as a senior escalation point for complex endpoint security issues.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Experience designing and delivering endpoint, systems, or corporate security solutions in environments that require scalable, durable controls.</li> <li>Deep knowledge of endpoint management platforms such as Jamf Pro or FleetDM, especially for architecting and securing macOS environments.</li> <li>Strong hands-on ability managed through Git repositories, merge requests, code review, and automated pipelines.</li> <li> Strong proficiency in scripting or programming for automation and security tooling, such as bash, You won't just support our people systems, you'll build them: owning the code, pipelines, and integrations that keep GitLab's People automation ecosystem running reliably at scale across Workato, Google Cloud, Claude, Workday, and the tools that power our global workforce. This is a strong fit if you think like a software engineer first, write clean and maintainable code, and thrive at the intersection of people systems, AI, innovation, and automation engineering.</p> <p>In this role, you'll be the technical backbone of our People Technology team, designing, building, and maintaining the automations, agents, and integrations that connect Workday, Greenhouse, Slack, and internal tools. You'll be the go-to technical thought partner for the people group on complex engineering decisions, and your work will compound over time: fewer manual processes, stronger system reliability, and a People technology foundation that scales without friction.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li>Own the design, development, and maintenance of people system automations and integrations across Workato, Google Cloud Platform, Claude, Workday, Greenhouse and GitLab, writing reliable, well-tested code that runs at scale.</li> <li>Build and maintain integrations between Workday, Greenhouse, Slack, and internal tools using Workday Web Services (WWS) and Slack's API and Bot SDK, diagnosing failures proactively and driving uptime and reliability improvements across the automation stack.</li> <li>Write, version, and maintain automation code in Ruby (or comparable scripting languages) stored in GitLab, with clear documentation, code reviews, and disciplined change
